# Omni View Top World News
> **Democrats seized both chambers of Congress, reshaping Trump's final two years.**

**What You Need to Know:** Democrats seized both chambers of Congress, reshaping Donald Trump's final two years in office. Persian Gulf governments warned that another US-Iran war would be more destructive, while a Houthi siege has encircled Yemen's Taiz for 30 days. This edition also draws on the Omni View Omni View North America desk.

### The Ten
**Democrats win control of House and Senate: Key US midterms takeaways: Al Jazeera**
In the United States, Democrats have won both the Senate and the House of Representatives, taking control of Congress for the rest of Donald Trump's presidency, which France 24 described as his final two years. Not every seat is called. Al Jazeera, citing the Associated Press, reported Democrats on 228 House seats and leading in 34 more, a total that could pass 260 and would be their largest House strength since 1990, when they won 267; after the 2024 election Republicans held 220 House seats and Democrats 215. In the Senate, Democrats have won 54 seats and lead in another, while Republicans have won 44 and lead in one; control takes 51, and Democrats last had a majority this clear in 2008, when they won 56. It is the first time in 20 years a Republican president has lost both houses, after George W. Bush in 2006, and Democrats have already flipped 25 House seats, more than the 21 they took in 2008, including seats in Texas, South Carolina, Iowa, Michigan and Kansas. Al Jazeera also reported 28 Democratic governors to 20 Republicans, with two races uncalled, against 27 Republican and 23 Democratic governors after 2024. Hakeem Jeffries told supporters, "Today begins the great American comeback"; if colleagues keep him as House leader, he would be the first Black Speaker, succeeding Republican Mike Johnson. Abdul El-Sayed, the son of Egyptian immigrants, defeated Mike Rogers in Michigan and is the first Muslim elected to the US Senate; he is to be sworn in on January 3. Trump called him a "jihadist" without citing evidence, and El-Sayed told supporters they could turn "inshallah" into "alhamdulillah," adding, "For the right-wing ops, that just means 'praise be to God.'" Susan Collins, Republican senator for Maine for three decades, conceded to Democrat Troy Jackson and said it had been the "honour of my life" to serve 30 years. Trump said Democrats did a "good job," that he would accept the results, and that "Iran was a piece of it," while noting he would still have the power, as president, to veto legislation; he also said that in some cases Republican candidates "were not my friend." Voters decided 145 ballot questions in more than three dozen states: Missouri rejected a proposed amendment that would have limited most abortions, with the Associated Press putting the "no" vote at 55.5 percent, and rejected a 2025 congressional map with 61.8 percent voting no; Virginia wrote in a right to reproductive freedom covering the first two trimesters, and Nevada a right to abortion until fetal viability, generally after 21 weeks, while Idaho defeated a measure that would have created abortion rights in state law. France 24 reported Keisha Lance Bottoms became the first Black woman elected governor of Georgia, and Byron Donalds the first Black man elected governor of Florida.
Ranks: US voters and anyone bound by federal law, war policy and trade · who controls Congress, investigations and the veto fight · immediately, for the rest of this presidency Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/4/democrats-win-control-of-house-and-senate-key-us-midterms-takeaways?traffic_source=rss) · [bbc.co.uk](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cmr4y92rgd9po?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss) · [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/americas/20261104-us-voters-back-abortion-rights-and-reject-trump-s-gerrymandering-in-state-ballot-measures) · [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/press-review/20261104-blue-tsunami-in-us-midterms-pummels-gop-out-of-power) · [komu.com](https://www.komu.com/news/elections/missouri-2026-midterm-election-results-key-races-and-amendments/article_bfd35c26-3fac-4a11-8265-261b8410d127.html) · [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/4/rejecting-hate-abdul-el-sayed-wins-senate-seat-despite-racist-attacks?traffic_source=rss)

**Persian Gulf leaders fear a renewed U.S.-Iran war as diplomacy sputters: Los Angeles Times**
In Bahrain, diplomats at the Manama Dialogue warned that another round of fighting between the United States and Iran could be more destructive than the war the Los Angeles Times said began on February 28. Anwar Gargash, a presidential adviser in the United Arab Emirates, said the Iranian and American stands are far apart and that "if these positions are not bridged, then we have to worry about the worst," adding that regional states are seeking a "political offramp" in a "protracted crisis of no war, no peace." Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said governments must "push very hard in order to prevent the escalation," because a second round "will be more dangerous, more destructive and it will lead to nowhere," and because more fighting would affect food and energy security. President Trump has hinted he could launch "another little Operation Epic Fury" after Tuesday's midterms, referring to the US-Israeli operation that opened the war, but on Monday he wrote, "Iran wants a settlement, as soon as possible. It could happen!" Hours later, Iranian state media reported explosions on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, and the Associated Press quoted an unnamed US official saying the military had carried out "defensive strikes." The Times reported that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, after an inconclusive election last month, is said to be pressing Trump to finish off the Islamic Republic. Last week Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish officials flew to Tehran and met Iranian military officials; Qatar is leading talks on a de-escalation plan Tehran has presented and Trump has not accepted. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told the Islamic Republic News Agency it is up to the Americans to decide "whether they have the will to take the wise path of diplomacy or, as in the past, seek to drag the situation into aggression and military operations." He added, "If they dare to test us again," they "will receive a much more bitter and severe result than before," after a first round in which Iran struck American bases in the region with drones and cruise and ballistic missiles.
Ranks: people in Iran, Israel and the Gulf, plus food and energy buyers · whether talks hold or a second round starts · days to weeks, with strikes already reported Source: [latimes.com](https://www.latimes.com/world-nation/story/2026-11-04/persian-gulf-leaders-fear-renewed-u-s-iran-war-as-diplomacy-sputters)

**Houthis’ monthlong siege on Taiz creating hell for trapped Yemenis: Al Jazeera**
In Yemen, the Houthis' siege of Taiz has lasted 30 days and, Al Jazeera reported, has affected hundreds of thousands of people. The United Nations has repeatedly warned of a catastrophe inside the city, where food and medicine are becoming scarce. The blockade has affected the 1.5 million people in Taiz City and others in rural districts, including about 180,000 displaced people trapped by clashes along the main road between Lahj and Taiz. The siege tightened when the Houthis seized al-Turbah, in the far southwest of the governorate, cutting the city's main artery to Aden. The Houthis reached Taiz's outskirts in 2015 after pushing the government out of Sanaa in September 2014; their takeover of the western countryside has now encircled the city. Salah Ahmed Ghaleb al-Majidi, acting director of the governorate's Siege Affairs Department, called it "the worst catastrophic siege imposed on a Yemeni city since the war began in 2014," with food, fuel, medical supplies and water not reaching the city and rubbish piling up. He said cut roads are also keeping families from relatives. Ahmed al-Mikhlafi, whose name Al Jazeera shortened for security, returned from Umrah in Mecca to find himself stuck in the western countryside; he described nearly 20 new Houthi checkpoints and a stop about 15 kilometres from the city, where fighters ordered his vehicle to turn back because of clashes.
Ranks: about 1.5 million people in Taiz City, plus rural residents and about 180,000 displaced people · food, fuel, medicine, water and movement cut · now, one month into the siege Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/4/houthis-one-month-siege-on-taiz-is-creating-hell-for-yemenis-stuck-there?traffic_source=rss)

**Netanyahu’s political rivals seize on Democrats’ sweep, seeking his ouster: The Globe and Mail**
In Israel, a week after an election the Globe and Mail described as leaving Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing coalition without a parliamentary majority, his rivals seized on the Democratic capture of Congress as proof he had squandered generations of bipartisan American support. The same account said the coalition still performed well enough to deny his main opponent, Gadi Eisenkot, a clear path to unseat him. Unlike earlier Israeli leaders who courted both US parties, Netanyahu has openly backed Republicans. The Globe and Mail reported that support for Israel among Democrats and some Republicans wavered after Israel's assault in Gaza following the 2023 Hamas attack, and fell further after Trump and Netanyahu ordered a joint attack on Iran. Some Democratic candidates made criticism of American military aid to Israel a campaign argument. Trump, who had endorsed Netanyahu, made an election-day pledge to halt 4 billion US dollars in annual funding to Israel, which he said would take away a "bad talking point" used by Democrats. Yair Golan, head of the centre-left Democrats party, wrote that the US results "reveal just how toxic Netanyahu is among both Democrats and Republicans." Yair Lapid said "Israel cannot afford" for Netanyahu to remain, because "It endangers our security, it jeopardises our democracy, and it will ruin our standing on the global stage." Netanyahu has so far remained silent on the US vote.
Ranks: Israelis waiting on a government, and the US-Israel aid relationship · who can form a cabinet, plus a pledged halt to 4 billion dollars a year · now, with coalition talks unresolved Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/world/article-us-midterm-election-results-live-updates-november-4-2026/)

**30 million South Africans registered to vote across nine provinces: France 24**
In South Africa, local elections are being held on Wednesday across nine provinces. About 30 million people have registered to cast votes, France 24 reported. The economy is at the forefront of the election. The spotlight is on Gauteng, a province long plagued by governance challenges. Helen Zille, 75, is running for mayor of Johannesburg. The New York Times reported she is betting voters care less about race and more about public services. The Times also reported that she is needling the African National Congress in that bid. No result is in; the polls are the decision, not a forecast.
Ranks: about 30 million registered voters in South Africa · who runs local services, including in Johannesburg and Gauteng · votes being cast today Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261104-30-million-south-africans-registered-to-vote-across-nine-provinces) · [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/04/world/africa/johannesburg-mayor-elections.html)

**EU to lead talks on support for Ukraine with US, Nato, partners: The Guardian**
The European Commission will meet the United States, Nato and the World Bank on winter aid after strikes hit Kyiv, Zhytomyr and a vessel near Odesa.
Ranks: people in Ukraine facing winter · power stations and a cargo ship hit, aid talks opening · immediate Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/nov/04/eu-ukraine-russia-france-germany-us-nato-europe-latest-news)

**US contractor gave Ethiopia secrets to help kill Tigray fighters: BBC**
An Ethiopian-born American admitted sharing dozens of classified US documents with senior Ethiopian officials to help kill Tigray fighters.
Ranks: US secrecy rules and the record of Ethiopia's Tigray war · dozens of classified documents admitted shared · already admitted Source: [bbc.co.uk](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6y8lz73vmv7o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)

**U.K. Supreme Court Hears Challenge to Ban on Palestine Action: What to Know: The New York Times**
Britain's Supreme Court hears a challenge today to last year's designation of Palestine Action as a terrorist organisation.
Ranks: members and critics of Palestine Action, and UK protest law · whether the ban stands · the hearing is today Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/04/world/europe/palestine-action-ban-uk-supreme-court.html)

**Azerbaijan's central bank reserves rise 35.7% y/y to $15.4bn: IntelliNews**
Azerbaijan's central bank reserves rose 35.7 percent in a year, to 15.4 billion dollars.
Ranks: Azerbaijan's public finances · reserves up by more than a third · already recorded, year on year Source: [intellinews.com](https://www.intellinews.com/azerbaijan-s-central-bank-reserves-rise-35-7-y-y-to-15-4bn-481604/)

**Euro zone wage growth to rebound slightly next year, ECB says: Yahoo Finance**
The European Central Bank says euro zone wage growth will rebound slightly next year.
Ranks: euro zone workers and employers · a slight rebound the ECB projects · next year Source: [finance.yahoo.com](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/euro-zone-wage-growth-rebound-093415154.html)

### Both Sides: Should the NBA keep Rwanda's paid partnership while US military sanctions stand?
The question is whether the National Basketball Association should keep a paid partnership with Rwanda, including finals at Kigali's BK Arena, while United States sanctions on Rwanda's military remain. The army-funded APR club has already been withdrawn from the 2026 Basketball Africa League. Democratic Senator Jeffrey Merkley and Republican Senator Marsha Blackburn wrote on 23 October that the NBA risked "becoming complicit in sportswashing by accepting money from a Rwandan government that systematically abuses human rights," and asked, "What is the NBA red line for accepting money from foreign governments that commit human rights abuses?" Their best reason is that a league that speaks of justice cannot keep taking government money after Washington sanctioned the Rwandan army in March, accusing it of fuelling the war in the Democratic Republic of Congo, and last week sanctioned the defence ministry over support for the M23 group, which has seized large parts of the east. DR Congo has asked the NBA, European clubs and Formula 1 to end Rwandan campaigns, arguing the deals clean Rwanda's image while fighting continues. NBA deputy commissioner Mark Tatum said the team "had been withdrawn" after those earlier sanctions, and the club stays barred while the sanctions last. Rwanda's stated case is a denial: Rwanda denies backing the rebels. That denial, if accepted, undercuts the charge that the partnership launders a war role. What is not in dispute in the reporting is the commercial fact: Rwanda is an official league partner, has hosted all but one final and playoff series since 2021 in the 10,000-seat arena, and the NBA reportedly receives millions of dollars a year. APR, third in 2024 and 2025, was replaced this year by the RSSB Tigers. The senators' 2 November deadline for a written answer has passed. The team remains out for as long as the sanctions stand; the articles do not set a date for ending or keeping the Kigali finals. Source: [bbc.co.uk](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c699zdx9knmpo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)

### Progress Watch
In Kenya, Food4Education now serves more than 600,000 school meals a day across 19,000 schools, with parents in some cases paying 5 Kenyan shillings, about 3 US cents, and about 80 percent of the food coming from small-scale farmers. DW reported that data show children at participating schools miss fewer classes and perform better, and that founder Wawira Njiru, 35, is receiving this year's German Africa Prize; the organisation has 6,000 staff, more than 70 percent of them women. Source: [dw.com](https://www.dw.com/en/wawira-njiru-kenya-s-no-1-school-feeder-honored-with-the-german-africa-prize/a-79646537?maca=en-rss-en-world-4025-rdf)

# Omni View Top World News
> **At least 29 are dead and 48 missing after Russia bombed a Ukrainian aid site.**

**What You Need to Know:** At least 29 people are dead and 48 are missing after Russia bombed an aid site in southern Ukraine, on a day when Americans are voting on control of Congress and Washington has told Congress it intends to end duty-free access for South Africa and Rwanda. US forces also struck Iran’s Qeshm Island while mediators kept a draft deal in circulation. This edition draws on 1 of the 5 Omni View regional desks live by press time.

### The Ten
**Russia bombs aid centre and shelter in Ukraine, killing at least 29 people: The Guardian**
In Ukraine, Russia bombed an aid distribution centre and a neighbouring shelter in Komyshuvakha, a village in the southern Zaporizhzhia region, killing at least 29 people, with 48 still missing. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia launched 289 attack drones, 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles across nine regions, triggering emergency power cuts, and that the barrage coincided with the US elections. He said the Russians think America will not notice this signal, and that Ukraine needs help defending its skies or Russia will never stop its missile strikes. The guided-bomb attack first hit a school building used to distribute humanitarian aid, then a nearby shelter. Mykhailo Semikin, acting head of the regional military administration, said the dead included four police officers and two rescue workers, that at least five people were hurt, and that Russian drones launched further attacks that hindered rescue work on Monday evening. In the north-east Kharkiv region, local authorities said a combined missile and drone attack wounded at least 62 people, damaged a medical facility in the Nemyshlianskyi district, shattered windows in four apartment buildings and damaged cars; Oleh Syniehubov, head of the regional military administration, said more than 200 patients were transferred. In the Dnipro area, local authorities said an attack killed one person and wounded 17, and rescuers pulled a woman alive from the rubble on Tuesday morning. As night fell in Komyshuvakha, emergency responders used torches to search collapsed buildings, according to photos and video posted by local officials. Zelenskyy called the Komyshuvakha attack vile and said it showed Vladimir Putin does not want to de-escalate; he said residents remaining there gathered each week for aid packages, and that Moscow was killing people rather than building on last week’s ceasefire in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, brokered by US first lady Melania Trump. The Kremlin said no other similar missions were being planned at the moment. That pause was the longest in the war, now in its fifth year, which has killed hundreds of thousands and displaced millions. US special envoy Steve Witkoff said US-led talks were due on 10 and 11 November in Abu Dhabi; the Guardian reported that Kyiv and its European allies worry Donald Trump has increasingly sided with Moscow.
Ranks: People at a Ukrainian aid site and across nine regions · at least 29 dead, 48 missing, power cuts and damaged hospitals · already, with talks dated 10-11 November Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/03/russia-bombs-ukrainian-aid-centre-komyshuvakha)

**Voters head to the polls as control of Congress is on the ballot: The New York Times**
In the United States, voters began heading to the polls on Tuesday in midterms that will decide which party controls Congress for the final two years of President Trump’s second term. All 435 voting House seats are contested; The Guardian reported that Republicans are defending a narrow majority and that Democrats need a net gain of four seats to take the House. Thirty-five Senate seats are up, 33 in regular elections and two special elections in Florida and Ohio; Republicans hold 53 seats, Democrats and independents who caucus with them hold 47, and Democrats need four seats for a majority, The Guardian reported. Voters are also choosing governors in 36 states and three US territories, plus thousands of state legislative seats and ballot measures on taxes, abortion rights and voting rules. The New York Times reported that President Trump has urged supporters to act as if he is on the ballot and has insisted Republicans would win if his base turned out, while Democratic campaigns have blamed his policies for the struggles of Americans trying to make ends meet, and Republicans have tried to frame the choice as one against opponents they cast as radical, far-left activists. A final New York Times and Siena University poll, published on Sunday, put Democratic candidates ahead in five of seven key battleground contests, including Texas and Kansas, where voters have not sent a Democrat to the Senate since 1988 and 1932, respectively, The Guardian reported. The Times reported that early voting has broken recent midterm records, with more than tens of millions of ballots already cast, that early turnout exceeded the last midterm cycle in each major Senate battleground, and that the share of registered Democrats rose in the early vote in several key states. It also reported that this is the most expensive midterm in political advertising since at least 2018, according to AdImpact, and that Elon Musk contributed $474 million to Republican candidates and their allies, more than any donor has spent in a single cycle. In Michigan, Democratic congresswoman Haley Stevens, who lost her party’s Senate primary to Abdul El-Sayed, endorsed his Republican rival, Mike Rogers, on Sunday, The Guardian reported. The president’s party has lost House seats in 18 of the past 20 midterms, a 90 percent rate of loss back to 1946, The Guardian reported. The first polls close at 7 p.m. Eastern, and the Times said full results could take days or weeks; in Texas, the Texas Tribune reported, domestic mail-in ballots postmarked by election day count if they arrive by 5 p.m. on 4 November, while military and overseas ballots must be postmarked by election day and received by 9 November.
Ranks: Voters across the United States · control of Congress for two years, plus 36 governorships · polls are open today; full counts may take weeks Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/live/2026/11/03/us/midterms-2026-election-day-trump/heres-the-latest) · [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live/2026/nov/03/midterm-elections-live-updates-voting) · [apps.texastribune.org](https://apps.texastribune.org/features/2026/texas-general-election-live-results-2026/)

**US hits Qeshm Island, Pezeshkian signals more diplomacy: Iran war latest: Al Jazeera**
In Iran, US forces struck Qeshm Island late on Monday, the first attack there since June, in what officials called a defensive measure, as both sides kept military and diplomatic tracks open. Iran’s state news agency IRNA said the blasts came in rapid succession and that witnesses saw two planes over the island, off Iran’s southern coast along the Strait of Hormuz. The Wall Street Journal, quoting an unnamed official, said the Monday-night strikes appeared limited and were not a resumption of a major operation; France 24, citing the Journal and unnamed US officials, described the hit on the largest island in the strait as the latest in a series of limited strikes Washington has secretly carried out in recent weeks, even as President Trump signalled progress in talks. The Associated Press quoted an unnamed US official as saying Washington conducted the strikes against Iranians using surface-to-air missiles against US assets. IRNA reported that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps had destroyed a US MQ-9 drone east of the Strait of Hormuz. Al Jazeera reported that the strikes came even as Vice President JD Vance described progress in talks. The war began on 28 February, when the United States and Israel launched strikes across Iran, closing the strait, sending oil and gas prices up and damaging military, civil and energy sites around the Gulf; on 7 March the United States struck a desalination plant on Qeshm, which Tehran called a flagrant crime against civilians and which cut freshwater to 30 surrounding villages. Qatari mediators have passed messages in indirect talks, but those talks appeared to end on Monday with no breakthrough, Al Jazeera reported. An official briefed on the talks told Reuters that Iran’s delegation left Doha on Sunday while a draft was still circulating, and that Qatari mediators travelled to Tehran on Monday night to meet Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on a draft under negotiation for eight days. Araghchi told IRNA that consultations through mediators are very intensive, that Iran has presented its conditions and proposals, and that everything depends on the political rationality of Washington. Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said the ball was in the US court, that Iran’s demands were clear and logical, and that a plan submitted in September could be shortened and implemented in two days, including reopening the Strait of Hormuz and returning to talks on Iran’s nuclear programme. President Masoud Pezeshkian said Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei had given the government certain authorities over talks with the United States, and that Tehran would look to resolve the conflict through dialogue.
Ranks: People around the Gulf and users of oil and gas through Hormuz · a limited strike while a draft deal is still circulating · already, with mediation ongoing Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/3/us-hits-qeshm-island-pezeshkian-signals-more-diplomacy-iran-war-latest) · [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsfeed/2026/11/3/us-conducts-series-of-defensive-strikes-against-iran?traffic_source=rss)

**Trump to remove Rwanda and South Africa from US trade deal: BBC**
In South Africa and Rwanda, President Donald Trump has notified Congress that he intends to remove both from the African Growth and Opportunity Act from 1 January 2027. The programme lets eligible African countries export thousands of products to the United States duty-free. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said an annual review found that both countries were engaging in practices inconsistent with the programme’s eligibility requirements, that both governments had been notified, and that the administration is working to ensure African partners meet those criteria. The administration cited barriers to US trade and investment and concerns over national security and foreign policy; for South Africa, it pointed to corruption. In a letter to President Cyril Ramaphosa, Trump said Pretoria’s actions on international security and its cooperation with governments of concern to Washington risked undermining US national security and foreign policy interests, and he accused South Africa of significant barriers to American trade and investment, including on agricultural market access, regulatory requirements, investment protections and intellectual property. Trade Minister Parks Tau called the decision unfortunate, said Washington was raising new issues that had not featured in negotiations begun in 2025, and said South Africa would accelerate diversification of export markets to protect jobs. Government figures he cited show about 89 percent of South African exports to the United States entered under ordinary World Trade Organization most-favoured-nation terms in 2025, while about 10 percent benefited from Agoa, down from 28 percent in 2024, and that the value of exports under the programme fell to about $1.7 billion in 2025 from $4 billion the year before. Bilateral trade reached $28.8 billion in 2025, and more than 600 American companies operate in South Africa, supporting about 134,600 jobs. Pretoria says South Africa supplies 12 of the 50 minerals the United States considers critical, and 70 percent of American isotopes used among other things in cancer treatment, and that South African manufacturers use American inputs in vehicles and boats exported under Agoa. US Ambassador Leo Brent Bozell III wrote on X that it was regrettable South African policies led to termination from Agoa, and that the outcome was predictable and preventable after the government rejected concerns raised by the United States. For Rwanda, Washington also raised human rights, political pluralism, the rule of law and workers’ rights. The BBC reported that the announcement comes amid strained relations, and that last year Trump accused South Africa of persecuting its white minority, launched a programme for white Afrikaners to seek asylum in the United States, and repeated claims of a genocide of white South Africans that the BBC described as widely discredited.
Ranks: Exporters and workers in South Africa and Rwanda · duty-free access to the US market · from 1 January 2027 Source: [bbc.com](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c9j346xg0mkvo)

**HKMA hosts fifth Global Financial Leaders’ Investment Summit: Hong Kong Monetary Authority**
In Hong Kong, the main session of the Global Financial Leaders’ Investment Summit ended on Tuesday, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority said. About 280 global financial leaders attended, including around 120 group chairpersons and chief executives, from banks, securities firms, asset owners, asset managers, private equity and venture capital firms, hedge funds and insurers. This year’s theme is “Rethinking the Playbook.” Vice Premier of the State Council He Lifeng delivered the opening keynote by video. Chief Executive of the Hong Kong SAR John Lee gave a keynote, and Financial Secretary Paul Chan delivered remarks. HKMA Chief Executive Eddie Yue said it was the fifth consecutive year of the summit, a platform for high-level dialogue, and that participants could see how Hong Kong is rethinking its playbook through innovation and technology while strengthening its position as an international financial centre. Panels discussed macroeconomic trends, market shifts and technological advances, and whether the financial playbook needs a major update in a world where risk is constant and resilience cannot be taken for granted. The South China Morning Post reported that banking leaders voiced confidence in the city as a bridge between mainland China and the rest of the world and as a safe haven helping businesses and investors navigate geopolitical tensions and shifting capital flows. Jean Lemierre, chairman of BNP Paribas, said European companies operating in Asia were increasingly seeking local funding and currency-hedging capabilities to manage volatility. The meeting began on Monday with a welcome dinner at The Henderson and ends on Wednesday with the “Conversations with Global Investors” forum co-organised by the HKMA, the Securities and Futures Commission and the Hong Kong Academy of Finance. The HKMA said the session was live-streamed.
Ranks: Banks and firms using Hong Kong for cross-border capital · a fifth summit and stated confidence, not a new law · forum ends 4 November Source: [hkma.gov.hk](https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2026/11/20261103-4/) · [scmp.com](https://www.scmp.com/business/china-business/article/3373156/amid-global-uncertainty-top-bankers-back-hong-kongs-role-mainland-chinas-gateway)

**Drones Emerge as the Top Killer of Civilians in Sudan’s War: The New York Times**
In Sudan, the United Nations says drones are this year’s top killer of civilians, in a population already overwhelmed by famine and drought.
Ranks: Civilians in Sudan’s war · drones are this year’s top cause of civilian deaths · already this year Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/03/world/africa/sudan-drone-civilians-nyala.html)

**Lebanon cuts power to public bodies as electricity crisis deepens: Al Jazeera**
In Lebanon, authorities have cut power to public bodies as political disputes and war deepen the electricity crisis.
Ranks: Public institutions in Lebanon · electricity cut off · now Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/3/lebanon-cuts-power-to-public-bodies-as-electricity-crisis-deepens?traffic_source=rss)

**Despite attacks, Saudi Aramco posts 34% rise in net profits in latest quarter: France 24**
In Saudi Arabia, Aramco said third-quarter profit rose 34 percent to $36.25 billion despite Houthi attacks on its sites.
Ranks: Saudi state oil revenue · profit up 34 percent to $36.25 billion · reported for the latest quarter Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/business/20261103-despite-attacks-saudi-aramco-posts-34-rise-in-net-profits-in-latest-quarter)

**Californians vote on billionaire tax to replace federal cuts in healthcare funding: France 24**
In California, voters are deciding Proposition 40, a one-time 5 percent tax on net worth above $1 billion, mostly for healthcare.

### Both Sides: Should the United States end Agoa access for South Africa and Rwanda?
What is being decided is whether South Africa and Rwanda stay in the African Growth and Opportunity Act, the programme that lets eligible African countries export thousands of products to the United States duty-free. President Donald Trump has notified Congress that he intends to remove both from 1 January 2027. The removal is an intention notified to Congress and to the two governments, not a change already in force.

The case for ending access, as the Trump administration states it, is eligibility. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said an annual review found practices inconsistent with the programme’s rules, and that the administration wants African partners to meet those criteria. For South Africa, Washington pointed to corruption, to barriers on agriculture, regulation, investment protection and intellectual property, and, in Trump’s letter to President Cyril Ramaphosa, to Pretoria’s security actions and ties with governments of concern to Washington. US Ambassador Leo Brent Bozell III said South Africa’s exit was regrettable but predictable and preventable, because the government rejected concerns the United States had raised.

The case against, as South Africa’s government states it, is that the penalty is poorly matched to the trade. Trade Minister Parks Tau called the decision unfortunate and said Washington was raising new issues that had not featured in talks begun in 2025. He said South Africa would diversify export markets to protect jobs. Government figures he cited put Agoa’s share of exports to the United States at about 10 percent in 2025, down from 28 percent in 2024, and the value at about $1.7 billion, down from $4 billion, against $28.8 billion in bilateral trade. Pretoria also says it supplies 12 of 50 minerals the United States lists as critical, and 70 percent of American isotopes used among other things in cancer treatment. The next dated step in the articles is 1 January 2027, the date Trump gave Congress for the intended removal.

# Omni View Top World News
> **Egypt signed a one-billion-dollar World Bank loan as war lifts prices for its people.**

**What You Need to Know:** Egypt signed a one-billion-dollar World Bank loan as war lifts prices for its people. False nuclear warnings hit alert apps in Ukraine and Russia, Sudan asked the United Nations to act over drones it says came from Ethiopia, and federal election monitors are due in Pennsylvania on Tuesday.
This edition draws on 1 of the 5 Omni View regional desks live by press time.

### The Ten
**Egypt signs $1 billion World Bank deal as war compounds economic pressures: The National**
Egypt’s foreign minister, Badr Abdelatty, signed a $1 billion World Bank financing agreement on Sunday, the second of three concessional development-policy operations. The bank’s board approved it in May; it includes a $200 million British credit guarantee and is tied to reforms of state-owned enterprises, competition rules, tax collection and the cost of government borrowing. The bank said then that Egypt had endured two years of successive external shocks, and The National reports those pressures have deepened because the US-Israeli war on Iran has raised oil, shipping and insurance costs for a country that relies on imports. Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly told the Egypt Forum in late October that oil was trading around $110 a barrel, against $75 assumed in the budget, and that the government chose to absorb the gap “at this stage” rather than pass costs to citizens, borrow to cover them, or risk power cuts of six to eight hours a day. President Abdel Fattah El Sisi told the same forum that fuel and electricity prices were “completely uneconomic” and sold below cost. Finance Minister Ahmed Kouchouk put subsidies at 840 billion Egyptian pounds ($15 billion) this fiscal year, with borrowing costs adding about 20 percent and bringing the real bill near 1 trillion pounds ($17.9 billion). The dollar rose by almost 8 percent, from about 52 pounds at the start of October to a record above 56 pounds on October 26, and about $4 billion of foreign money is estimated to have left Egyptian government debt between October 15 and 26. Central Bank Governor Hassan Abdalla called a flexible exchange rate the “first line of defence” and said unifying the rate mattered more than the rate itself; on Thursday the bank raised rates by 100 basis points to 20 percent, the first increase since March 2024, and pushed its inflation target to late 2027. Trading halted for 30 minutes on October 25, the first suspension since 2021, after the EGX100 index fell 10 percent, while remittances hit a record $33.9 billion in the first eight months and Suez Canal income, near $10 billion a year before Red Sea attacks, has recovered only to about $4.4 billion.
Ranks: Egyptian households and the state budget · higher fuel, food and borrowing costs, plus a signed loan · already this autumn Source: [thenationalnews.com](https://www.thenationalnews.com/news/mena/2026/11/02/egypt-signs-1-billion-world-bank-deal-as-war-compounds-economic-pressures/)

**Nuclear radiation in Russia, Ukraine? No, just hacked warning alerts: Al Jazeera**
Ukraine’s Air Force said late on Sunday that users of its Air Alert app received fake warnings of a radiation threat, a chemical attack and street fighting in and around Kyiv, and of a Russian Oreshnik missile. One message was in Russian. Ukrainian authorities said within the hour that unauthorised parties had interfered and that the app had been taken offline, and the Air Force wrote that there was no radiation threat. Ukraine’s Center for Strategic Communications blamed Russia and pointed to the Russian-language message; the government said a separate app for the capital was working normally. Al Jazeera’s Audrey Macalpine, reporting from Kyiv, said speakers in the city centre also sounded the warnings and that most people understood within about half an hour that this was a hacking attack. The Guardian reported that the ministry took the app offline temporarily and said the wider system — texts, broadcasts, street sirens and loudspeakers — was still operating. Media reports cited by Al Jazeera said the Russian alerts warned of nuclear warheads on drones across all regions and told people to stock food for three weeks and hide. Al Jazeera said this appears to be the first time either country’s official alert app has been hacked, and that the fake threats began the same day a six-day local ceasefire in the Russian-occupied Kherson region ended, a truce the United States said was brokered by first lady Melania Trump.
Ranks: People who rely on official alert apps in Ukraine and Russia · false nuclear and chemical warnings, apps taken offline · Sunday night and Monday morning Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/nov/02/ukraine-russia-emergency-warning-systems-hack-zelenskyy-streeting-eu-latest-news-updates)
Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2/nuclear-radiation-in-russia-ukraine-no-just-hacked-warning-alerts)

**Sudan files complaints against Ethiopia with UN over deadly drone spree: Al Jazeera**
Sudan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said late on Sunday that it had lodged complaints with the United Nations Security Council and the African Union’s Peace and Security Council over drone attacks this year. The ministry accused the Rapid Support Forces of using Ethiopian territory to strike “civilian sites and power stations,” and said the incidents place Ethiopia before international law. Sudan’s military has repeatedly accused Ethiopia of aiding the RSF in a civil war under way since April 2023; Ethiopia has accused the Sudanese military of backing rebels linked to the Tigray People’s Liberation Front, a charge Khartoum denied. An army-led Transitional Sovereignty Council report alleged 70 assaults from February 15 to October 27 involving 187 one-way attack drones, saying the attacks killed or wounded 484 civilians, killed 176 soldiers and wounded another 200. The report said drones had taken off from Ethiopian soil since February 2026 and named launch sites at Asosa Airport, the Kurmuk-Gizen border area and Bahir Dar airbase. It said last month brought 28 attacks by 97 drones, and it cited an October 9 strike on displaced families in Wad el-Mahi that it said killed 30 civilians — 26 women and four children — and wounded 100. A spokesman for UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said on Saturday that Guterres was “appalled” and “strongly condemns the escalating drone attacks in Sudan by the parties to the conflict,” calling the strikes violations of international humanitarian law, days after another strike on a market in RSF-controlled Darfur killed more than 100 people.
Ranks: Civilians in the Sudanese cities named in Khartoum’s report · hundreds killed or wounded, on the army’s figures · since February, complaint filed Sunday Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2/sudan-files-complaints-against-ethiopia-with-un-over-deadly-drone-spree?traffic_source=rss)

**The DOJ plans to send poll monitors to Philly on Election Day. Here’s what we know: Inquirer.com**
The US Department of Justice plans to send election monitors to polling places in Philadelphia and in Allegheny, Luzerne and Lehigh counties on Election Day, according to an October 22 letter to Pennsylvania’s Department of State. Those counties include Pittsburgh, Allentown and part of Bethlehem. The department said the monitors’ job is to check compliance with the Voting Rights Act, the National Voter Registration Act, the Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act and other federal laws. Trial attorney James T. Catania wrote that monitors “only observe and take notes,” will not intrude, will identify themselves to each poll manager, will wear business casual clothes without DOJ insignia and will not carry firearms. The Inquirer, citing CBS News, reported that the department plans a record 1,000 monitors nationwide, up from 289 in the 2022 midterms and 714 in the 2024 presidential election. State Deputy Secretary Jonathan Marks told county officials there is no specific federal or state statute authorizing the monitors and that they have no greater access than the general public. A Department of State spokesperson said they may be inside polling locations but must stay at least 10 feet outside the area where voting machines are located, and Marks said they may not enter restricted areas, inspect equipment or demand records. Vic Walczak of the American Civil Liberties Union of Pennsylvania said the monitors are not a cause for alarm, and the Philadelphia mayor’s office assured people there was nothing to worry about; the Inquirer, citing Newsweek, reported that Indiana, Kentucky and one Arkansas county have told the department to remain outside.
Ranks: Voters in four Pennsylvania counties and a national monitor deployment · observers inside polls, kept from machines and records · Tuesday’s Election Day Source: [inquirer.com](https://www.inquirer.com/politics/election/department-of-justice-election-monitors-philadelphia-voter-intimidation-interference-20261102.html)

**Ryanair says it may freeze workers' pay and raise airfares: BBC World**
Ryanair is considering a temporary wage freeze for staff and said airfares will be “materially higher” next summer because fuel costs have jumped after the US-Israel war with Iran. The airline said it expects fuel prices to stay high well into 2027 unless there is a swift resolution, and it forecast its fuel bill €2 billion (£1.6 billion) higher in the short term. Chief executive Michael O’Leary said fares would have to rise by double digits to help cover the cost, and he repeated an earlier forecast that Ryanair would need a 20 percent fare increase to cover jet fuel. He said he was not sure the airline would get to 20 percent, but that he was looking at double-digit fare increases across Europe from all airlines in 2027. Pre-tax profits fell 16 percent to €2.4 billion in the six months to the end of September, which the airline linked largely to fuel costs that jumped 15 percent. Ryanair said 80 percent of its fuel bill had been hedged and that the cost of the rest was elevated, and it tied the surge in aviation fuel to a sharp cut in refined products from the Gulf. It said a pay freeze could start in April as multi-year wage deals end, and that it would use more artificial intelligence in back-office and support work.
Ranks: Ryanair staff and passengers flying in Europe · a possible pay freeze and double-digit fare rises · fares next summer, a freeze from April if adopted Source: [bbc.co.uk](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cr0qkve1x224o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)

### Both Sides: Should the NHS end Palantir's data-platform contract?
Britain’s health secretary, Yvette Cooper, faces calls to end Palantir’s contract for the National Health Service federated data platform, built to join scattered medical files, speed discharges and improve surgery scheduling. NHS England’s website says 137 trusts are live and lists 29 as “realising benefits” from the £330 million system. Those 29, in freedom-of-information replies gathered by the charity Medact, said the system is not live or that they are not using its applications. Epsom and St Helier said it was not using the platform at the moment. University Hospitals of North Midlands said it is not live and that the trust does not intend to roll it out.

Chi Onwurah, chair of the Commons science and technology committee, argues that if many trusts do not see the value, serious questions follow about whether the hype matches reality. She wants ministers to activate the 2027 break clause and open a competition for a supplier owned and based in the United Kingdom. The Commons health select committee is also calling for the deal to be pulled. Dr Rhiannon Mihranian Osborne of Medact says there is no good reason to continue what she calls a failing project.

Louis Mosley, Palantir’s UK and Europe chief executive, says ending the contract would be “putting politics above patients,” and he accuses critics of “Palantir Derangement Syndrome.” His case is that cancelling the firm would sacrifice the gains the platform is meant to deliver for patients. The Office for Statistics Regulation said it will take the “realising benefits” claim into its casework, after NHS England conceded it could not prove that 117,539 more operations at trusts using the platform were caused by it. Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/02/palantir-unused-nhs-hospital-trusts)

# Omni View Top World News
> **More than one hundred twenty ships hit since February now include a Qatari gas carrier struck Friday.**

**What You Need to Know:** More than one hundred twenty commercial ships have been hit since February, and on Friday unidentified objects struck the Qatari gas carrier Al Mayeda in the Gulf, with no crew injuries reported. The same weekend, youth-led cost-of-living protests drew more than 320,000 people in France and turned violent in several German cities. This edition draws on 1 of the 5 Omni View regional desks live by press time.

### The Ten
**Qatar LNG carrier struck by ‘unidentified objects’ in Gulf: Al Jazeera**
In Qatar, the Qatar Gas Transport Company said its liquefied natural gas carrier Al Mayeda was hit by “unidentified objects” while sailing in the Gulf on Friday evening. The company called it the latest attack on commercial shipping since the US-Israel war on Iran began in February, and it issued the statement on Sunday. The statement, published by the Qatar Stock Exchange, said none of the crew was injured and no environmental damage was reported. It said the vessel is in a safe condition and operational, and that the impact is being assessed. The company supplies Qatari ports and terminals with towage and marine support services. More than 120 commercial ships have been hit since the war began, according to data from the International Maritime Organization and the UK Maritime Trade Operations. Iran, which closed the Strait of Hormuz early in the war, has repeatedly warned that vessels trying to pass without its permission would face “destruction”. Attacks have increased since the United States reimposed a blockade on Iran’s southern ports in July; with at least 29 ships hit, October was the worst month, ahead of the 20 attacks recorded in March.
Ranks: Gulf commercial shipping and energy cargoes · Another strike inside a war that has hit more than 120 ships · Immediate, with damage still being assessed Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1/qatar-lng-carrier-struck-by-unidentified-objects-in-gulf)
Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1/qatar-lng-carrier-struck-by-unidentified-objects-in-gulf?traffic_source=rss)

**Shops looted as German cost of living protests turn violent: BBC World**
In Germany, rioters looted shops in central Frankfurt late on Saturday as clashes over the cost of living also broke out in Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg. Police said they used water cannons to disperse protesters targeting emergency workers with fireworks, stones and bottles. Frankfurt police said “violent riots” hit the city centre, that Molotov cocktails were thrown at emergency services, and that windows of a gun shop and other shops were smashed, with trainers stolen and two weapons seized after a suspect was arrested. Thousands had joined largely peaceful demonstrations earlier, organised by Gen Z regelt against underfunding in schools, the high cost of living, public spending cuts and military service. The BBC reported that more than 320,000 people also demonstrated in France on Saturday, a third consecutive weekend of largely peaceful protests over living costs and poor public services, especially education. Authorities in Frankfurt, Munich and Berlin reported as many as 18,000 protesters, roughly half the organisers’ website estimate, while German media said tens of thousands marched. Spokesperson Lina Friedrich said the demonstrations were “to fight for peace and freedom, rather than for war and coercion”, and that the group wants better health and education support, opposes compulsory military service, and favours a fairer distribution of the burden. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt told Bild that overnight police had prevented “violence like that seen in Paris” and called for “harsh punishments” for rioters and looters. Hesse interior minister Roman Poseck said “around 100 clearly identified left-wing extremists” infiltrated Frankfurt; Berlin police said 27 officers were injured and up to 56 people were temporarily detained, and Hamburg broadcaster NDR reported 120 arrests.
Ranks: Marchers, police and shopkeepers in German cities, plus French demonstrators · Looting, injuries and arrests beside a fight over schools, prices and military service · Already under way Source: [bbc.co.uk](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cqj34gnd3n30o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)
Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/hundreds-of-thousands-protest-in-france-for-act-iii)
Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/youth-led-rallies-sweep-europe)

**Bulgarians vote in presidential run-off amid Black Sea tensions: Al Jazeera**
In Bulgaria, voting is under way in a presidential run-off marked by regional security threats and domestic economic concerns. President Iliana Iotova, 61, led former caretaker prime minister Andrey Gyurov, 50, in the first round but fell short of the 50 percent needed to win. Election officials said the first round drew a record low turnout, with only 23 percent of eligible voters casting a ballot. Exit polls will be published after voting ends at 8pm, 18:00 GMT, on Sunday, with a result expected on Monday. The vote comes after a series of drone attacks on merchant ships off Bulgaria’s Black Sea coast in the past month. About two dozen seafarers are feared dead, and on Wednesday a Greek container ship sank after being hit by sea drones. Prime Minister Rumen Radev, who backs Iotova, said the strikes’ outcome “benefits the Russian Federation”; both leading candidates have condemned the attacks and called for a diplomatic end to the war in Ukraine. A win for Iotova would make her Bulgaria’s first elected female president; she became acting president in January after Radev resigned to enter and win a parliamentary race. Gyurov, backed by pro-Western reformist parties and by figures including former prime minister Boiko Borisov, signed a security cooperation agreement with Kyiv while premier and says he wants Bulgaria to be a reliable NATO ally.
Ranks: Bulgarian voters and Black Sea crews · An undecided presidency beside attacks in which about two dozen seafarers are feared dead · Result expected Monday Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1/bulgarians-vote-in-presidential-run-off-amid-black-sea-tensions)

**Pakistan, Saudi Arabia push for early signing of GCC free trade agreement: Profit by Pakistan Today**
In Pakistan, Commerce Minister Jam Kamal Khan and Saudi Arabia’s new ambassador, Dr Rajeh Albugamy, discussed early signing and implementation of a proposed Pakistan-Gulf Cooperation Council free trade agreement. The minister said the proposed agreement could expand market access and create opportunities for Pakistani exporters. He tied the talks to Saudi Vision 2030 and to Pakistan’s industrial capacity, and he pointed to cooperation on production, product quality, technology and private-sector partnerships. Pakistan and the GCC concluded negotiations in September 2023, but the agreement has yet to be formally signed and implemented. Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar said in October that the agreement was nearing completion, with approval potentially pending from one GCC member state. The ambassador reaffirmed Saudi commitment to economic ties and highlighted agriculture and regional connectivity. Both sides agreed to keep coordinating on trade, investment and agricultural cooperation. The proposed deal would cover Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait and Oman. The meeting, described in a statement issued on Saturday, did not itself sign the agreement.
Ranks: Pakistani exporters and six GCC markets · A finished negotiation still unsigned · Follow-up agreed, signing date not set Source: [profit.pakistantoday.com.pk](https://profit.pakistantoday.com.pk/2026/11/01/pakistan-saudi-arabia-push-for-early-signing-of-gcc-free-trade-agreement)

**Tommy Robinson conviction leaves far right with leadership void: The Guardian World**
In Britain, a jury at Southwark crown court found far-right activist Tommy Robinson, whose real name is Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, guilty of harassment causing fear of violence to two journalists. Deliberations took more than 11 hours. The prosecution said he used “bullyboy, intimidatory tactics” against Daily Mail reporters Andrew Young and Jacob Dirnhuber after they reported on his alleged role influencing the 2024 Southend riots. Robinson admitted “paying” for the personal number of Daily Mail editor Ted Verity and left a message threatening to make the paper’s journalists and their families “famous”. He potentially faces up to 10 years in prison and will learn his sentence on 16 December. Anti-migrant activist Daniel Thomas, known as Danny Tommo, whom the Guardian described as the obvious heir apparent, is in custody ahead of a trial over the alleged slashing of a dinghy in the Channel. Joe Mulhall, director of research at Hope Not Hate, said there is “definitely a leadership void in the anti-migrant space”. Restore Britain leader Rupert Lowe, the MP for Great Yarmouth, wrote that the system had treated Robinson unfairly. Robinson thanked Elon Musk for bankrolling his legal expenses and told supporters one day at Southwark court cost £20,000.
Ranks: Two journalists and Britain’s anti-migrant organising scene · A conviction, with a possible prison term and no clear successor named · Sentence on 16 December Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/nov/01/tommy-robinson-conviction-leaves-far-right-with-leadership-void)

**Election Day is Tuesday. What you need to know to vote in NC’s 2026 midterms: WRAL**
Around one-third of North Carolina’s eligible voters have already cast midterm ballots, and Tuesday’s polls run from 6:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m.
Ranks: Remaining North Carolina voters · A shortened in-person window · Tuesday Source: [wral.com](https://www.wral.com/news/nccapitol/how-to-vote-nc-north-carolina-voter-guide-sample-ballot-find-precinct-november-2026/)

**Yamaha boycotts Qatar Grand Prix amid ongoing Middle East war: Motorsport.com**
Yamaha will not send its factory or Pramac teams to the Qatar Grand Prix at Losail on 6-8 November, citing company travel restrictions.
Ranks: Yamaha’s MotoGP riders and the Doha round · A missed race · Next weekend Source: [motorsport.com](https://www.motorsport.com/motogp/news/yamaha-to-boycott-qatar-grand-prix-amid-ongoing-middle-east-war/10870537/)

**Indonesia and Uzbekistan Create Committee for Food Security and Trade: London Daily News**
Indonesia and Uzbekistan agreed a joint committee on food security, trade and investment, while a free-trade deal and dried-fruit imports remain unfinished.
Ranks: Two governments’ trade officials · A coordination body, not operating projects · Not dated Source: [londondaily.news](https://www.londondaily.news/indonesia-and-uzbekistan-create-committee-for-food-security-and-trade/)

**Georgia voters want and deserve a free, fair and accurate election: The Atlanta Journal-Constitution**
More than 2.8 million Georgia voters cast midterm ballots in early voting that closed Friday, ahead of Tuesday’s governor and Senate races.
Ranks: More than 2.8 million Georgia voters · A closed early-voting record · Tuesday Source: [ajc.com](https://www.ajc.com/opinion/2026/11/georgia-free-fair-election-day-voting/)

**Rachel Reeves says UK’s future is in EU as she backs Andy Burnham on Brexit: The Guardian World**
Rachel Reeves said Britain’s future should be back in the EU, since Brexit has made the UK poorer, weaker and less secure.
Ranks: British voters and firms tied to EU trade · An argument from a former chancellor, not a new law · Not dated Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/nov/01/rachel-reeves-uk-future-is-in-eu-andy-burnham-brexit)

### Both Sides: How Germany should answer the cost-of-living protests
Saturday’s marches have left Germany’s government and the organisers arguing over what the state should do next: punish the night’s violence, or move on the spending, schools and military-service demands that brought people out in daylight.

Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt’s case for punishment starts with the harm already done. He told Bild that overnight police had prevented “violence like that seen in Paris” and called for “harsh punishments” for rioters and looters. Shops were looted in Frankfurt, emergency workers were targeted, Berlin police reported 27 officers injured, and Hamburg broadcaster NDR reported 120 arrests. Hesse interior minister Roman Poseck said “around 100 clearly identified left-wing extremists” infiltrated Frankfurt and that France must not be held up as a model. Cologne police chief Johannes Hermanns said extremists who had “nothing but violence in mind” had entered a march by young people who wanted to demonstrate peacefully.

Gen Z regelt spokesperson Lina Friedrich’s case starts with what the daytime crowds asked for. She said the demonstrations were “to fight for peace and freedom, rather than for war and coercion”, and that what matters most is better support for health and education, opposition to compulsory military service, and a fairer distribution of the burden. Thousands joined largely peaceful demonstrations before the clashes. The same day, the BBC reported, more than 320,000 people demonstrated in France over the cost of living and public services, especially education.

No article names a dated vote on those demands. Arrests and the punishments Dobrindt wants are the next official step these reports actually describe. Source: [bbc.co.uk](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cqj34gnd3n30o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)

**Binance customer recovery after the hack**
Crypto firm Binance is covering 90 percent of losses after a 6.3 billion dollar hack. The FBI says North Korea was responsible for the hack. That coverage is a completed repayment pledge with a measured share, not a plan to investigate later. # Omni View Top World News
> **More than 20,000 California mail ballots stay counted after courts blocked a federal set-aside.**

A second Friday order limits prosecution threats against election workers, with voting set for November 3. This edition draws on 1 of the 5 Omni View regional desks live by press time.

### The Ten
**Court Rejects Latest Trump Effort to Impound California Ballots: The New York Times**

In the United States, Friday brought two court losses for the Trump administration’s attempt to intervene in California’s elections, with voters going to the polls on Tuesday, November 3.

The New York Times reports that a federal appeals court again refused an order that would have made California officials set aside more than 20,000 mail-in ballots. The court called that notion unconstitutional. Late the same Friday, a federal judge temporarily stopped the Justice Department from threatening election officials with criminal prosecution if they decline to follow the department’s directives on ballots. The Times says the administration could now ask the Supreme Court to step in.

The Times treats the lawsuit as one piece of a wider push, built up over recent weeks, to raise doubts about whether the vote will be counted fairly. It ties that push to voter discontent and to what it describes as President Trump’s sagging approval ratings. It also says Republican candidates are struggling to keep an edge in a series of red states before Tuesday, while the administration looks to the courts for what the Times calls a structural advantage.

The Justice Department has widened its California investigation by sending federal grand jury subpoenas to local election officials. The Times describes that expansion as an effort to prove claims, which it calls unsubstantiated, that thousands of noncitizens sit on the state’s voter rolls. The union that represents California election workers sued over those subpoenas. Its filing accuses the department of “unprecedented and unlawful threats” that “risk interfering with the lawful administration of the ongoing 2026 midterm elections and the counting of ballots.”

The same live report carries a separate Justice Department move in Alaska. On Thursday the department issued dozens of subpoenas linked to what the Times calls a Democratic plan to stack the ballot in a close Senate contest that could help decide which party controls the chamber. Democratic candidate Mary Peltola said late Thursday that she had not known about the effort. The Times had reported that operatives aligned with her campaign aimed to recruit extra candidates in order to peel votes from Republican Senator Dan S. Sullivan. At a fund-raiser in Juneau on Thursday night, Peltola said: “I knew nothing about any other candidates on the ballot except for me and the incumbent. That is all I have ever known about. I am not interested in tricking voters.” Her former campaign manager, Elisa Rios, told the Times that Peltola was not directly part of the ballot-packing effort but was “definitely aware.” Those two accounts sit in the same article and do not agree.

Campaign travel is also moving. A White House official told the Times that Trump will hold rallies in Kansas and Iowa on Sunday. The paper calls that a sharp reversal: the rallies had been canceled a day earlier in two states it describes as traditionally Republican, where polls indicate tight races. On Friday Trump said he had wanted to try tele-rallies in those states, and that Republicans in both had called to say an in-person visit would be better.

Other named campaign stops sit in the same report. Former President Bill Clinton was scheduled to appear on Friday in Tupelo, Mississippi, for Senate candidate Scott Colom. Former Vice President Kamala Harris will deliver the keynote at a Democratic fund-raising dinner in Fulton County, Georgia. In South Carolina, the Times reports, the contest between Republican Senator Darline Graham and Democratic challenger Dr. Annie Andrews is effectively tied.

France 24, in a separate report, says Americans vote on November 3 in midterms that could see Republicans lose control of Congress and put President Trump’s legislative agenda in danger. It notes that the Constitution leaves the running of elections to the states, and that this has not stopped the president from trying to use his influence before the vote. Jonathan Diaz, director for voting advocacy and partnerships at the Campaign Legal Center, told France 24 that the administration has tried to insert the federal government into almost every aspect of the election process. Diaz said the long-term risks are very significant, and that even if the president has not succeeded in changing the rules or in coercing state and local officials, the effort has created an atmosphere of fear and uncertainty.

France 24 cites a new poll by the Associated Press-NORC Center for Public Affairs. In that poll, 55 percent of Democrats said they are confident the final count after the midterm will be accurate, compared with 38 percent of Republicans.

France 24 reports that Trump has repeatedly claimed large numbers of noncitizens vote in United States elections, while the figures it cites show this is exceedingly rare. Voting is already limited to citizens and already requires identification. A noncitizen who tries to vote can face fines, prison, or deportation. France 24 says even think tanks that support Trump’s voting restrictions have failed to find evidence of widespread fraud. It quotes an April New York Times account of the Heritage Foundation’s database: 100 documented cases of noncitizens voting from 1982 to 2025, about 0.000008 percent of more than 1.3 billion votes cast in presidential elections across that span.

The bill Trump is pressing is the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act, which would require documentary proof of United States citizenship in order to vote. The United States does not issue a national identity card. Under the act, a driver’s license or other official identification would not be enough if it does not show a place of birth. France 24 lists the documents that would count: a valid United States passport, a military identification card, a valid government-issued photo identification showing the person was born in the United States, or a birth certificate, but only if that certificate matches the person’s current name exactly. France 24 says the exact-name rule could be a problem for the 69 million women who changed their names after marriage, and for the trans community.

The Campaign Legal Center, as cited by France 24, says more than 21 million Americans, or nearly 10 percent of voting-age Americans, lack access to documentary proof of citizenship. It names young people, people in lower income brackets, and people of color as the groups most affected. A 2024 report by the Center for Democracy and Civic Engagement, also cited by France 24, found that 3 percent of people of color lack proof such as a birth certificate, a passport, or naturalization documents. By comparison, 1 percent of white Americans have no such documentation. France 24 reports that only 1 percent figure in the sentence that follows the 3 percent finding.

A Republican amendment to the legislation also aimed to limit voting by mail or online, by rebuilding those systems so they comply with the stricter identification rules. The bill passed the House of Representatives in February and then languished in the Senate for lack of support. France 24 says Trump’s allies are still trying to move it through the budget reconciliation process. It also reports that last year the administration expanded the Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements database, known as SAVE, which exists to check whether someone is a citizen and therefore qualifies for government benefits. The expansion allowed states to use that database to check whether someone is eligible to vote.

The Guardian, in a third report dated the same day, says government corruption has emerged as a key issue for midterm voters and points to what it calls an exclusive poll. The article frames its examples as alleged self-dealing, not as a court finding. It writes that the Qatari government gifted Trump a luxury jet, potentially violating the emoluments clause of the Constitution. It writes that the United Arab Emirates gained access to some tightly guarded, high-end American artificial-intelligence chips soon after an investment firm linked to its ruling family secretly bought a 500 million dollar stake in World Liberty Financial, the crypto company funded by the families of Trump and Steve Witkoff. It writes that people facing criminal charges have taken to donating to Trump’s political operations and then seeking pardons or clemency. Most recently, it says, Wanda Vázquez Garced, the former governor of Puerto Rico, and Julio Herrera Velutini, whom the Guardian describes as the banker who paid her bribes, were pardoned after Velutini’s family gave a 50 million dollar deal to Alina Habba, Trump’s former personal lawyer, and donated 3.5 million dollars to Trump’s Maga Inc super PAC. The Guardian also writes that the Pentagon lent more than 600 million dollars to Vulcan Elements, a rare-earths startup, three months after Donald Trump Jr.’s venture capital firm, 1789 Capital, bought a stake in the company. It further writes that Powerus, a drone maker backed by Eric Trump and Donald Trump Jr., is selling drone interceptors to Persian Gulf allies of the United States that are under attack by Iran.

For voters and election workers in California, the immediate change is that the mail ballots the administration wanted set aside remain in the count, and that prosecution threats tied to the department’s ballot directives are blocked for now. The national electorate votes on Tuesday. The next legal step the Times names is a possible request to the Supreme Court. In Congress, the citizenship-document bill is still not law.

Ranks: California voters and election workers, and the national midterm electorate · ballots kept in the count and prosecution threats blocked, with Congress still at stake · before voting on Tuesday, November 3 Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/live/2026/10/30/us/midterms-elections-trump)
Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/americas/20261031-united-states-atmosphere-of-fear-trump-moves-to-curtail-voting-rights-ahead-of-the-midterms)
Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/31/trump-government-corruption-midterms-voters)

### Both Sides: Documentary proof of citizenship to vote
Congress is deciding whether a voter must produce documentary proof of United States citizenship before casting a ballot. President Trump is pressing the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act. France 24 reports that the bill cleared the House in February and then stalled in the Senate, and that his allies still want it attached to budget reconciliation.

The case Trump is making, as France 24 reports it, is that large numbers of noncitizens are voting and that identification already required at the polls is not a sufficient check. His stated reason is that the franchise belongs to citizens. The administration has already widened the SAVE database so a citizenship test built for benefits can be used by states on voter rolls. Documents the bill would accept are a valid passport, a military identification card, a government photo identification that shows birth in the United States, or a birth certificate whose name matches the voter’s current name exactly. A Republican amendment would also rebuild mail and online voting around those same papers.

The case against, from Jonathan Diaz at the Campaign Legal Center, is that the administration has not rewritten the rules for this midterm but has produced fear and uncertainty among the officials who run the count. The center’s numbers, cited by France 24, say more than 21 million Americans, nearly one in ten voting-age adults, cannot produce the papers, with the burden falling on the young, people on lower incomes, and people of color. The 2024 Center for Democracy and Civic Engagement report puts the share without a birth certificate, passport, or naturalization papers at 3 percent among people of color and 1 percent among white Americans. France 24 also notes that an exact-name birth certificate could shut out many of the 69 million women who took a new name after marriage. On the fraud claim itself, France 24 points to the Heritage Foundation database, via an April New York Times report: 100 noncitizen-voting cases from 1982 through 2025, about 0.000008 percent of more than 1.3 billion presidential votes in those years. It says think tanks that favor the restrictions have still not found fraud on a wide scale.

The next step is in the Senate, not on a court calendar. The bill is not law, and allies are still seeking a reconciliation route. Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/americas/20261031-united-states-atmosphere-of-fear-trump-moves-to-curtail-voting-rights-ahead-of-the-midterms)
