# Omni View Top World News
> **One Houthi drone aimed at Mecca was destroyed Friday, Saudi Arabia says, a claim Houthis deny.**

**What You Need to Know:** Saudi Arabia says a Houthi drone aimed at the Mecca region was destroyed on Friday, a claim the Houthis deny as other intercepts were reported across the kingdom. Manila and Washington set new alliance steps as an independent Russian paper said it was being forced to close, and crews searched for six people after a helicopter crash in northern India. This edition draws on 1 of the 5 Omni View regional desks live by press time.

### The Ten
**Saudi Arabia reports interception of Houthi drone targeting Mecca: Al Jazeera**
In Saudi Arabia, the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said it intercepted a drone the Houthis launched toward the Mecca region. Coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki said in a social media post that the drone was intercepted and destroyed on Friday morning. It was also reported that a missile aimed at western Saudi Arabia was brought down earlier. Al-Malki said on Friday that the coalition’s air defences intercepted and destroyed a Houthi cruise missile that targeted western Saudi Arabia. On Thursday, the coalition said it destroyed a ballistic missile fired by the Houthis toward the kingdom’s eastern region. It later said two ballistic missiles launched toward the Saudi capital, Riyadh, were also intercepted and destroyed. A Houthi spokesperson denied targeting the Muslim holy city or the surrounding region, and said the group’s cross-border attacks remain strictly focused on Saudi energy and military infrastructure. The spokesman wrote that operations target Saudi oil facilities and military bases, and that no one believes what he called fabrications and lies propagated by the Al Saud regime. The coalition has previously accused the Houthis of launching drones toward Islam’s two holiest cities, Mecca and Medina. Al Jazeera reported that hostilities between the Riyadh-backed Yemeni government and the Iran-backed Houthis continue to escalate, that attacks have continued with no sign of slowing, and that humanitarian agencies warn of worsening conditions for civilians.
Ranks: people in the Mecca region and across Saudi Arabia · a reported drone strike on a holy-city region, denied by the Houthis · Friday, with further intercepts the same week Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/30/saudi-arabia-reports-interception-of-houthi-drone-targeting-mecca?traffic_source=rss)

**The Philippine archipelago on the front line of China’s territorial ambitions: The Globe and Mail**
In the Philippines, US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth met Secretary of National Defense Gilberto Teodoro Jr. on October 28, the US Mission to ASEAN said. The two discussed progress on security cooperation, alliance modernization and posture initiatives. They agreed to launch an alliance command and control modernization sprint to enhance real-time bilateral coordination and strengthen alliance resilience. They also welcomed progress operationalizing the bilateral Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement sites, including investments in critical infrastructure and storage facilities across the Philippines. Secretary Hegseth announced an increase in the Department of War’s security cooperation funds to accelerate modernization of the Armed Forces of the Philippines and enhance interoperability along the First Island Chain. The Globe and Mail reported that Teodoro has separately said Manila needs to increase access by air and sea to Batanes, the northernmost province, and that there will be a multidomain deployment of military assets to the islands. Teodoro told the paper that in any Taiwan contingency, Philippine waters and Batanes may be affected, and that Manila includes that in its defence calculations. Batanes covers about 200 square kilometres, about a third the size of the Greater Toronto Area, and sits in the middle of the Luzon Strait, which connects the Pacific Ocean to the South China Sea. The islands do not have a large permanent garrison, owing to their environmentally protected status and a propensity for being struck by super typhoons. In June, 20 Tao people rowed nearly 200 kilometres from Taiwan’s Orchid Island to Batanes in a narrow 12-metre wooden boat painted white and red, a crossing the paper said had not been made in 300 years. Proto Galarion, a cultural worker in Mahatao on the main island of Batan, where the boat is now displayed, said the trip was meant to respect the historical relationship and that Batanes is part of the Philippines. Some in China have used those historic links to suggest Batanes’s three populated islands and smaller islets and atolls should be under Chinese control. The Globe and Mail said discussion of Batanes has so far been limited to Chinese academia and state media, with Beijing’s government remaining silent. Teodoro said the recent noise is concerning because it echoes Beijing’s approach in the South China Sea, which began with historical claims before territory was seized and Filipino fishermen were pushed out of traditional waters. In 2016 an international tribunal ruled much of China’s claims unlawful, but Beijing has refused to budge, and clashes between Chinese and Philippine coast guard and fishing vessels are becoming more common around Scarborough Shoal and the Spratly Islands. The Philippines is a US treaty ally, with Washington required to come to Manila’s aid if it is attacked.
Ranks: people in the Philippines and US forces along the First Island Chain · more alliance funds, a command sprint, and a stated plan to increase military access to Batanes · announced this week; no invasion date given Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/world/article-batanes-philippine-front-line-of-chinas-territorial-ambitions-taiwan/) · [asean.usmission.gov](https://asean.usmission.gov/readout-of-secretary-of-war-pete-hegseths-meeting-with-philippine-secretary-of-national-defense-gilberto-teodoro-jr/)

**Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta to close, citing pressure from ‘special services’: The Guardian**
In Russia, the independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta announced on Friday that it is closing, citing pressure from authorities. Editor-in-chief Sergei Sokolov said in a video statement published on YouTube that Novaya Gazeta is ceasing to exist and that the Russian authorities, the Russian special services, have forced the editorial team to end its work. He said Novaya Gazeta has been killed, and that on November 9 the newsroom will turn off the lights in the home where it has lived for 30 years, shut down the servers and leave. The paper cited authorities who recently searched the home of its senior editor and earlier this year detained one of its journalists. This month Sokolov was taken in for questioning and Russian authorities searched his home over a criminal case involving colleague Oleg Roldugin, who was arrested in April. Roldugin was detained and charged with unlawful access to computerised information, without any details being given, and pleaded not guilty, according to the state RIA news agency. He is awaiting trial under house arrest that has been extended until November 10, according to Novaya Gazeta. Moscow classes the paper a foreign agent, a label used to stifle dissent. Russia has introduced near-Soviet levels of censorship since sending troops to Ukraine, pushing the vast majority of independent journalists into exile. Novaya Gazeta cut down production inside Russia after the offensive began in February 2022, and authorities revoked its media licence the same year. The paper’s then editor-in-chief, Dmitry Muratov, jointly won the Nobel peace prize in 2021 for his efforts to safeguard freedom of expression at the helm of the paper. France 24 also reported the closure, describing Novaya Gazeta as one of the last vestiges of independent journalism in Russia and citing the search of the senior editor’s home and the detention of a journalist earlier this year.
Ranks: Novaya Gazeta’s newsroom and its readers in Russia · the paper says it will shut its servers on November 9 · days Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/30/novaya-gazeta-russia-independent-newspaper-to-close) · [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20261030-russia-s-bastion-of-free-press-novaya-gazeta-shuts-down-after-years-of-kremlin-pressure)

**Rescue operations on after Indian helicopter crashes in Himalayan state: BBC World**
In India, a search for survivors is under way after a helicopter carrying six people, including five pilgrims, crashed in the northern Himalayan state of Uttarakhand, officials say, BBC World reported. Uttarakhand’s Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami said the helicopter had crashed near a village close to Joshimath in Chamoli district. Rescue teams have been dispatched to the mountainous area, but the condition of those on board remains unclear. The aircraft reportedly took off from the Hindu pilgrimage site of Badrinath on Friday afternoon before losing contact. The cause of the crash is not yet known. The incident happened amid reports of heavy rain and poor visibility, and India’s weather department had issued an orange alert for the area, warning of thunderstorms, hail and strong winds. Dhami said a joint rescue operation was under way involving the district administration, the disaster management department and the State Disaster Response Force. He said he is continuously monitoring the entire incident, and that he had ordered that anyone seriously injured be airlifted for treatment. Uttarakhand borders China and Nepal, is home to some of Hinduism’s holiest shrines, and attracts millions of pilgrims every year. Badrinath is one of four sacred sites on the Char Dham pilgrimage circuit, alongside Kedarnath, Gangotri and Yamunotri, and many devotees travel through steep Himalayan valleys to temples open for only part of the year because of harsh winter conditions. Helicopter services have become increasingly popular among pilgrims seeking to avoid difficult mountain journeys, but their safety has come under scrutiny following a series of accidents. In June 2025, seven people were killed when a helicopter carrying pilgrims crashed near Kedarnath, and another seven died in a crash on the same pilgrimage route in October 2022. Several other helicopter accidents were reported during the 2025 pilgrimage season, prompting aviation authorities to tighten safety checks and restrict some operations.
Ranks: six people on the flight and their families in Uttarakhand · a mountain crash with rescue still under way · now Source: [bbc.co.uk](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cr93zxyn9eqeo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)

**UK house prices grow at slowest pace in two years as mortgage rates rise: The Guardian**
In Britain, house prices grew by an annual rate of just 0.5 percent in October, the slowest pace in more than two years, as higher mortgage rates put off potential buyers, The Guardian reported. The average price for a property in the UK stood at £273,566 in October, according to the lender Nationwide. That average was flat on the previous month. Annual growth was down from 0.8 percent in the year to September. Nationwide is the source of the October reading, the monthly comparison and the September comparison. For buyers, the lender pointed to higher mortgage rates as the reason the yearly pace cooled. For owners, the average price Nationwide published did not move from the prior month.
Ranks: buyers and owners in the UK housing market · annual growth slowed to 0.5 percent, with the average flat on the month · October’s reading Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/oct/30/uk-house-prices-grow-at-slowest-pace-in-two-years-as-mortgage-rates-rise)

**Spain demands answers as train disaster toll rises: France 24**
In Spain, the toll from Wednesday’s high-speed collision south of Madrid rose to 69 dead, with scores injured, as officials demanded answers, France 24 reported.
Ranks: families of the dead and injured in Spain · toll now 69 · already Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261030-spain-demands-answers-as-train-disaster-toll-rises)

**Oil flows are up as Iran war turmoil eases. Why do prices keep rising?: Al Jazeera**
Gulf crude exports averaged 24.6 million barrels a day in the week to October 18, above the pre-war average, yet Brent briefly topped $117 on Friday, more than 60 percent above pre-war levels, Al Jazeera reported, with October the deadliest month for attacks on commercial vessels, 32 incidents logged by UKMTO.
Ranks: oil buyers worldwide · Brent briefly above $117, more than 60 percent above pre-war · Friday’s market Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/10/30/oil-flows-are-up-as-iran-war-turmoil-eases-why-do-prices-keep-rising)

**PBOC reveals overnight rate at 1.25% before policy anchor shift: The Edge Singapore**
In China, the People’s Bank of China revealed an overnight rate of 1.25 percent before a policy-anchor shift, The Edge Singapore reported.
Ranks: borrowers and banks in China · overnight rate shown at 1.25 percent · before the anchor shift Source: [theedgesingapore.com](https://www.theedgesingapore.com/news/china/pboc-reveals-overnight-rate-125-policy-anchor-shift)

**Bayer wins Roundup weedkiller cancer trial while awaiting settlement ruling: Reuters**
In the United States, Bayer won a trial over claims Roundup caused cancer in three women, while awaiting a settlement ruling, Reuters reported.
Ranks: Bayer and the three women in the trial · a defence win, settlement still pending · ruling awaited Source: [reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/world/bayer-wins-us-trial-which-it-was-alleged-that-roundup-caused-cancer-three-women-2026-10-30/)

**How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam: BBC World**
Kenyans are among those charged in an alleged $130 million US student-aid scheme that used stolen identities, BBC World reported.
Ranks: US student-aid funds and people whose identities were allegedly used · an alleged $130 million scheme, with Kenyans charged · charges already filed Source: [bbc.co.uk](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cxvgdzpy7241o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)

### Both Sides: Was a Houthi drone aimed at Mecca?
The question is whether a drone the Saudi-led coalition says it destroyed on Friday was aimed at the Mecca region. Coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki said the aircraft was intercepted and destroyed Friday morning after the Houthis launched it toward that region. The coalition’s case is that the intercept fits a pattern it has already described: it has previously accused the Houthis of sending drones toward Mecca and Medina, and it reported further intercepts around the same days, including a cruise missile aimed at western Saudi Arabia, a ballistic missile toward the eastern region on Thursday, and two ballistic missiles toward Riyadh. The Houthi spokesperson’s case is a denial that the group targeted the holy city or the surrounding region. He said cross-border attacks remain strictly focused on Saudi energy and military infrastructure, wrote that operations target oil facilities and military bases, and called the Mecca allegation a fabrication and a lie propagated by the Al Saud regime. Al Jazeera’s account does not include independent tracking that would settle the flight path. What the reporting does date is the sequence: the eastern-region missile and the two Riyadh missiles on Thursday, the Mecca-region drone and the western cruise missile on Friday, with humanitarian agencies warning that conditions for civilians are worsening as the exchanges continue and attacks show no sign of slowing. Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/30/saudi-arabia-reports-interception-of-houthi-drone-targeting-mecca?traffic_source=rss)

# Omni View Top World News
> **Three hundred thousand people lose fishing income as Iran's war idles most boats in two provinces.**

A Texas lawsuit seeks to block certification of the November 3 midterms, and Spain's transport minister ties the Toledo crash, now at least sixty-nine dead, to a computer failure and a normal-speed restart. This edition draws on 1 of the 5 Omni View regional desks live by press time.

### The Ten
**War in the Middle East continuing to disrupt Iran’s fisheries sector, with estimated millions in losses: SeafoodSource**
In Iran, the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs says the Middle East war has heavily disrupted fisheries in Hormozgan and Bushehr, two of the country’s top commercial fishing provinces. OCHA estimated direct and indirect losses in those provinces at around 105.9 million US dollars, or 94.4 million euros. More than 60 percent of the fishing fleet there remains inactive, directly cutting the income of an estimated 37,000 fishers and causing other harm to the livelihoods of an estimated 300,000 people. Hamzeh Rostampour, head of Iran’s Fisheries Organization, put the damage at more than 60 trillion Iranian rials, about 33.1 million US dollars or 29.5 million euros, a smaller total than OCHA’s. OCHA said communities that lost fishing assets, facilities, and post-harvest infrastructure, including damage to a major shrimp hatchery in Bushehr, have no clear indication of when meaningful production might restart or when fishers would be allowed time to recoup losses. The Food and Agriculture Organization is assessing the needs of conflict-affected fisheries in southern Iran, and FAO representative Farrukh Toirov said the agency is providing emergency support through its Technical Cooperation Program to restore essential fishing capacities, support affected coastal communities, and strengthen household food security. The World Forum of Fisher People, a 29-member group that says it represents at least 10 million small-scale fishers, said its members listed fuel as up to 50 percent of operating costs, and that Iran’s restrictions on the Strait of Hormuz, a chokepoint for roughly 20 percent of the world’s oil, lifted Brent crude from around 70 US dollars a barrel before the conflict to above 100 and as high as 119. WFFP said diesel and gasoline costs have risen 60 to 120 percent in many markets since late February, and SeafoodSource reports that the European Union, the United States, Thailand, and Ecuador have been enabling fuel aid for commercial fishers. Despite the conflict, Iran’s Fisheries Organization has moved forward with plans to inaugurate 122 fisheries projects across 23 provinces.
Ranks: about 300,000 people in two Iranian provinces · fishing income cut and boats mostly idle · already underway Source: [seafoodsource.com](https://www.seafoodsource.com/news/war-in-the-middle-east-continuing-to-disrupt-iran-s-fisheries-sector-with-estimated-millions-in-losses)

**Texas elections aren’t official until they get certified. Here’s how it works.: The Texas Tribune**
In the United States, the Potter County Republican Party in the Texas Panhandle filed a lawsuit on October 27 seeking to block certification of the November 3 midterm elections unless all machine-cast paper ballots are counted by hand. The Texas Tribune reports that the suit, without providing proof, warned of potential interference from artificial intelligence and foreign adversaries such as China. Jonathan Diaz, director of voting advocacy and partnerships at the Campaign Legal Center, said certification is a ministerial duty, mandatory, with no discretion, and that by then officials have already completed the post-election checks required by state law. Joshua Blank, research director of the Texas Politics Project at the University of Texas at Austin, said the Texas Election Code states that public officials “shall certify the tabulations,” an obligation rather than a choice. Kenneth Parreno, counsel at Protect Democracy, said voting-rights advocates are watching because state and federal officials have spread disinformation about who is voting, but that under the code those officials should not and cannot refuse a valid count. The code already requires a portion of paper ballots to be hand-counted to verify machine tabulations, and it makes it a felony if someone knowingly or intentionally refuses to count votes the person knows are valid or alters a report to exclude them. Parreno said failing to certify canvassed results would violate that provision, and that if an official declines, state law says candidates and voters may be entitled to a court order to prevent the violation. Certification is the last step of canvassing, which includes tabulating ballots and verifying the count, and a certificate of election is granted weeks after election night. The governor, House speaker, and county commissioners play a role by race, and local canvassing authorities, typically a county commissioners court, certify local contests such as city council and mayor, with experts saying they have little to do beyond approving the results.
Ranks: Texas midterm candidates and voters · a bid to halt official results · before certification after November 3 Source: [texastribune.org](https://www.texastribune.org/2026/10/29/texas-election-certify-how-it-works/)

**Treasury denies Healey plan to cut welfare bill before election, claiming his comments were misinterpreted – UK politics live: The Guardian**
In Britain, The Guardian reports that the Treasury denies a John Healey plan to cut the welfare bill before the election and says his comments were misinterpreted. Healey denied postponing difficult decisions on the welfare system and said the government is making changes now. He said the system was broken, that face-to-face assessments were put back in place starting two years ago, and that universal credit terms were changed so people do not have to brand themselves as too sick to work. He said he and the prime minister have argued that the cost of benefits has to come down in the long run, but not by crude cuts while people feel cost-of-living pressure. Interviewer Robinson put a 19-billion-pound rise in the year ahead against the entire police budget for England and Wales and the entire annual defence equipment budget, and asked whether any of the cuts would come before the next election. Healey said two big reports next month will help map long-run change, then a white paper and legislation, and that the rate of increase in the welfare bill has been reduced over the last two years compared with what he called a broken system the Conservatives put in place. He said there will be a reduction in the benefits bill. Thinktanks and opposition parties have said the difficult decisions are being postponed, the claim Healey rejected on GB News.
Ranks: people on UK benefits · a promised smaller bill, timing disputed · reports due next month Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/politics/live/2026/oct/29/budget-john-healey-labour-uk-politics-latest-news)

**Hope floats on Louisiana’s shrimp boats, despite dire economic times: The Globe and Mail**
In the United States, Louisiana shrimpers are still enlarging boats while the Gulf and South Atlantic catch loses value. The Globe and Mail reports that the value of the domestic shrimp catch fell 65 percent between 2000 and 2024, from about 738 million US dollars to nearly 258 million US dollars. Captain Ronnie Anderson, 59, known as Chevo and vice president of the Louisiana Shrimp Association, is investing around 100,000 US dollars to lengthen his 81-foot trawler, Last of the Mohicans, so it can hold 80,000 pounds, after he estimates he has already spent 400,000 US dollars on the boat since buying it. The upgrade has taken more than two months of around-the-clock work at the Gulfbound shipyard in Bayou Little Caillou, which Lucy Pinell, 58, co-owns with her husband Randall, 61. Anderson told the Globe the industry’s turn came after European restrictions in 2002 on Asian shrimp found with prohibited antibiotics sent rejected shrimp into US markets, and that industrial aquaculture now supplies inexpensive shrimp. The Globe reports that a flood of imported shrimp, rising fuel and operating costs, and dwindling profits have driven fishermen to sell boats, leave the trade, and discourage their children from following them. Pinell said she wants the shrimping culture to stay. The paper says controversies over President Donald Trump’s immigration policies, what it calls his attacks on American democracy, and the war in Iran do not resonate in these communities, which have stayed loyal to him. Anderson, who has shrimped since childhood in Buras and whose boat was the only shrimping vessel in his hometown not destroyed in Hurricane Katrina, said he expects to survive and wants a next generation in the trade.
Ranks: Gulf and South Atlantic shrimpers · catch value down about two-thirds since 2000 · already, with boats still being rebuilt Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/world/article-midterms-us-2026-louisiana-shrimp-boats-mississippi-river/)

**Pakistan, Turkmenistan discuss transit trade deal and transport corridors: Trend News Agency**
In Pakistan, lawmakers and Turkmenistan’s ambassador discussed putting a transit trade agreement to work, not a pact signed on Thursday. Trend News Agency reports that Sanjay Perwani, head of Pakistan’s Parliamentary Friendship Group with Turkmenistan, met Ambassador Atadjan Movlamov at Parliament House in Islamabad. A National Assembly press release said the talks focused on expanding bilateral trade and on finalising and operationalising the Pakistan-Turkmenistan Transit Trade Agreement, particularly because Turkmenistan is landlocked and needs reliable transit routes. The sides also stressed regional transport corridors to improve connectivity and facilitate trade. Pakistan has been seeking a role as a transit and maritime gateway for landlocked Central Asian countries through the ports of Karachi, Port Qasim, and Gwadar on the Arabian Sea. In July 2026, President Asif Ali Zardari and Kyrgyz President Sadyr Zhaparov stressed multimodal transport and greater use of Pakistani seaports, and their joint statement reaffirmed existing agreements on transport, logistics, and transit. In September 2025, Pakistani officials discussed with a Kazakh delegation road, rail, and maritime corridors linking Central Asia with the Arabian Sea, including port operations and free trade zones. Trend reports that any practical benefit for Turkmenistan would depend on implementation, transit arrangements, and whether the routes are reliable and competitive.
Ranks: traders in Pakistan and landlocked Turkmenistan · a transit pact still not operational · no start date named Source: [trend.az](https://www.trend.az/casia/turkmenistan/4240684.html)

**What we know so far about deadly Spain train crash: BBC**
In Spain, minister Óscar Puente says controllers restarted trains at normal speed after a computer failure, and at least sixty-nine people died.
Ranks: more than 540 passengers · at least sixty-nine killed · already, line still stopped Source: [bbc.co.uk](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cm8xz7pkd0jjo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)

**Humanitarian aid set to enter Oleshky as a rare Russia-Ukraine truce holds for a third day: WRAL**
In Ukraine, both sides say a fifty-four-hour truce still holds so aid can reach about two thousand people in Oleshky on Friday.
Ranks: about 2,000 people in Oleshky · food and medical aid if the truce holds · Friday Source: [wral.com](https://www.wral.com/news/ap/aab99-humanitarian-aid-set-to-enter-oleshky-as-a-rare-russia-ukraine-truce-holds-for-a-third-day/)

**Israel election results live: Netanyahu accused of ‘ugly delegitimisation campaign’ after his claims about Arab parties: The Guardian**
In Israel, police dismissed Likud’s claim that parties representing Palestinians stole the election, while absentee ballots are still being counted.
Ranks: Israeli voters and party blocs · a theft claim rejected by police · during the ongoing count Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/oct/29/israel-election-results-live-updates-poll-netanyahu-eisenkot-bloc-coalition-latest-news)

**Brazilians split over Flavio Bolsonaro’s exit to US: Al Jazeera**
In Brazil, Al Jazeera says people are split after Flavio Bolsonaro left for the United States and refused to concede to President Lula.
Ranks: Brazilian voters · a refused concession and a departure · already Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsfeed/2026/10/29/brazilians-split-over-flavio-bolsonaros-exit-to-us-2?traffic_source=rss)

**North Koreans being recruited into forced labour in Russia, report says: Al Jazeera**
In Russia, a Global Rights Compliance report says a Russian broker network is recruiting North Korean labourers on student visas.
Ranks: North Korean workers recruited to Russia · forced labour via student visas, scale unstated · as the report describes it Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/10/29/north-koreans-being-recruited-into-forced-labour-in-russia-report-says?traffic_source=rss)

### Both Sides: Should India open farm markets in a US trade deal?
India and the United States have not signed the trade pact whose framework they unveiled in February, a framework that brought down President Donald Trump’s punitive tariffs on most Indian goods. What is being decided is whether the first phase, which New Delhi says is nearly final, gives American farm goods new access to India.

Trade minister Piyush Goyal said in New Delhi on Thursday that India will not compromise the interests of its farmers or other stakeholders, and that once details are out Indians will celebrate that not a single sensitive farm or stakeholder interest was compromised. His stated reason is that a finished text can protect those interests and still leave India with a strong advantage.

The Samyukt Kisan Morcha, a coalition of more than 100 farm groups, said earlier this month that the deal put farmers for sale because it eliminated India’s high tariffs on maize, almonds, walnuts, apples, and soybean oil, among other products. Farming groups have repeatedly asked the government to share more of the text, arguing that imports of subsidised US farm products could depress domestic prices and hurt rural incomes. The union says it will organise further demonstrations in November to protest the deal and seek its withdrawal.

The next dated step the groups have named is those November demonstrations. The two governments have not signed off on the pact. Source: [centraloregondaily.com](https://www.centraloregondaily.com/news/nation-world/india-says-trade-deal-with-us-will-not-hurt-its-farmers/article_0a067e51-3941-5aee-bbe8-788319f4a182.html)

# Omni View Top World News
> **Exit polls give Arab parties up to 18 seats and no Israeli bloc a majority.**

The Pentagon's latest accounting of the Iran war, a deadly high-speed crash in Spain, and an Ebola toll of almost 5,000 deaths sit behind that count. This edition draws on 1 of the 5 Omni View regional desks live by press time.

### The Ten
**Rivals in Israel Election Strike Tone of Triumph, but Outcome Is Far From Clear: The New York Times**
In Israel, voters turned out Tuesday in the largest numbers in a generation, and exit polls left Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's alliance roughly even with the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot. The New York Times reported that the election did not immediately decide who would lead next, and that counting was expected to last days, followed by a potentially lengthy effort to assemble a parliamentary majority. If those polls hold, neither bloc can form a government without two Arab parties projected to take 17 or 18 seats in the 120-seat parliament, which the paper called their strongest showing ever. Netanyahu effectively ruled those parties out of a coalition, and Eisenkot and his partners have balked at including them too. France 24 reported that Arab-led parties appear to have made a historic showing, and that it is not clear whether other opponents of Netanyahu's government would join them for a majority. Eisenkot is a former military chief whose son was killed in the Gaza war. Past midnight, he told supporters, "Tonight we got the answer: The public wants change." Hours later, Netanyahu said it was clear Likud was the largest party, mocked months of polls that had shown his party trailing Eisenkot's, invoked his relationship with President Trump and his case for removing what he calls the threat of Iran, and declared, "We must form a strong right-wing government." The Times said Netanyahu has led the most far-right government in Israeli history, and that Eisenkot has called him unfit to lead. Analysts are already weighing whether the two could join in a unity government; the paper said that path faces major obstacles, because Eisenkot's voters despise Netanyahu and the two would have to agree on who serves as prime minister. After official totals, President Isaac Herzog is to invite the leader he thinks can build a coalition, usually at least 61 lawmakers; Eisenkot has floated a minority government. The Jerusalem Post reported that with more than 4 million votes counted, Netanyahu was pulling ahead of Eisenkot, and that exit polls projected nine seats for Yair Golan's Democrats, potentially more than doubling that party's representation. The same paper reported that Winter and Hendel were both projected to fall short of the 3.25 percent threshold needed for any Knesset seats. The Guardian reported that far-right national security minister Itamar Ben-Gvir's Otzma Yehudit was expected to remain on six seats, the same as in 2022, and that his watch party met the exit polls in stunned silence. Hundreds of thousands of ballots from military bases, hospitals, prisons and embassies were still outside the exit polls; last time those votes favored Netanyahu's coalition, and Israel's exit polls have a spotty record in tight races.
Ranks: Israeli voters and the next governing coalition · neither bloc has a majority on the exit polls · official totals and coalition talks follow days of counting Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/live/2026/10/27/world/israel-elections)
Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261028-israelis-await-final-election-results-as-netanyahu-remains-far-from-defeated)
Source: [jpost.com](https://www.jpost.com/israel-election-2026/article-913053)
Source: [jpost.com](https://www.jpost.com/israel-election-2026/article-913064)
Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/oct/28/israel-election-results-live-updates-exit-polls-netanyahu-likud-eisenkot-latest-news)

**Mind-Boggling True Cost of Trump’s War on Iran Revealed: The Daily Beast**
In the United States, the Pentagon told Congress that taxpayers had spent at least $47.1 billion on the Iran war through October 16, The Daily Beast reported, nine months into a conflict President Donald Trump had said would last weeks. Congressional officials shared that bill with The New York Times; it is $3.5 billion above the accounting six weeks earlier, and officials told the Times the estimate is almost certainly low. Munitions are $29 billion of the total. Replacements and repairs are $6.1 billion. The Air Force has spent $7.6 billion operating several squadrons and hundreds of sorties. The Army's tab is $2.1 billion for bases in the region, and the Navy's is $1.5 billion, with about 20 ships in the Middle Eastern theater at a time. The Pentagon also listed $92 million for moving supplies, $14 million for cyber operations, $24 million for medical costs, and $645 million for elite commandos. CENTCOM says 50,000 troops are involved. The Daily Beast reported that many Army bases are understood to have come under intense Iranian airstrikes, and that The New York Times found repair costs for those bases were not in this bill. A Congressional Research Service report this month said 80 aircraft had been lost or damaged; the Pentagon said the war has cost 18 American lives and left about 860 people injured. Heavy use of munitions is slowing Patriot shipments to Ukraine, and President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine had waited nearly a month for Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to sign off on missiles for Patriots and NASAMS. In June the White House and the Pentagon asked Congress for another $70 billion. Major strikes are paused while Trump decides whether to resume them after next week's midterm elections. Yahoo reported that he told a rally in Lubbock, Texas, the war would end "whenever I want it to," and that he will soon decide whether to "make a deal" with Iran or "finish it off." The same report said The New York Times had reported that U.S. and Israeli militaries drew up plans for a short but intensive operation against Iran after the midterms, and that the United States evacuated diplomats from Saudi Arabia earlier this month.
Ranks: U.S. taxpayers, deployed forces, and Ukraine's air-defense queue · at least $47.1 billion through October 16, plus 18 American deaths · ninth month, with a strike decision after the midterms Source: [thedailybeast.com](https://www.thedailybeast.com/mind-boggling-true-cost-of-trumps-war-on-iran-revealed)
Source: [yahoo.com](https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/donald-trump-says-iran-war-091748099.html)

**Africa’s ‘unprecedented’ Ebola outbreak could reach UK, says top health official: The Guardian**
In Africa, the current Ebola outbreak has reached 10,000 cases and almost 5,000 deaths, The Guardian reported. Dr Jean Kaseya, director general of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, called that spread unprecedented. He warned the illness could reach the United Kingdom and other countries. He said that risk holds unless more funding is secured for preparedness and possible treatment. He compared the outbreak to Covid, which first took hold in China before crossing borders, claiming millions of lives and ravaging health systems and economies.
Ranks: patients in the outbreak and health systems that could be next · 10,000 cases and almost 5,000 deaths · Kaseya says spread can continue without more funding Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/oct/28/africa-ebola-outbreak-could-reach-uk-says-top-health-official)

**Two high-speed trains collide in Spain, halting traffic on Madrid-Andalusia line: France 24**
In Spain, at least ten people have died in a crash between two high-speed trains Wednesday morning in Toledo province, France 24 reported. Esther Padilla, speaking for the Castilla-La Mancha government, told state broadcaster TVE that both trains were heading from Madrid to Seville and that one ran into the tail of the other while it was stopped, knocking two cars off the track. She told local media there are at least 10 dead and that the number may increase. Rail operator Adif said the collision was between Mora and Orgaz, on the line between Madrid and Seville, and suspended traffic on the Madrid-Andalusia high-speed line, including service between Madrid, Ciudad Real and Andalusia. A regional government spokesperson said a Renfe train and an Iryo train crashed just after 9 a.m., with 397 passengers on the Renfe train and 147 on the Iryo train, and that the cause and the number of injuries were still being determined. The Guardian reported that Spain's state broadcaster said a high-speed train ran into the back of another service and knocked two carriages off the track. Footage on regional Castilla-La Mancha Television showed a derailed train, at least one carriage still on an elevated section, and twisted metal and wreckage on the embankment below. France 24 said El País cited witnesses describing numerous injuries, with two rail cars leaving the tracks and falling down an embankment. Government sources told El País the crash could be worse than the January disaster near Adamuz, on the same line and between trains of the same operators, that killed 46 people. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez wrote on X that he was shocked, said he remained in contact with the transport minister and the president of Castilla-La Mancha, and offered solidarity to the victims and their families. The opposition People's Party cancelled its campaign events; leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo said the priority is to attend to the victims and support their families. Spain's main parties, preparing for next month's general election, suspended planned activities, and the prime minister's published agenda was cleared for the day. Manuel Galán, mayor of Urda, near Toledo, said emergency services asked him to prepare a sports hall for the injured.
Ranks: the dead, the injured, and passengers on the Madrid-Andalusia line · at least 10 killed and the high-speed line stopped · rescue and a rising toll are today's work Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20261028-two-high-speed-trains-collide-in-southern-spain-rail-operator-says)
Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/28/spain-train-crash-high-speed-toledo)

**Kim Jong Un tells commanders to prepare for war as border tensions rise: UPI**
In North Korea, Kim Jong Un told army company leaders on Tuesday to get their units fully ready to fight a war, the official Korean Central News Agency reported, as UPI relayed from Seoul. He said the primary revolutionary task of those leaders is to round off combat preparations of their units, and he called for a radical improvement in strenuous, intensive training. He praised company leaders as the foundation of the military's strength. Defense Minister Kim Song Gi, military chief of staff Ri Yong Gil, and Pak Jong Chon, vice chairman of the Workers' Party Central Military Commission, joined him. Kim had chaired the company leaders' meeting in Pyongyang on October 22 and 23, the first army-wide gathering since the party's ninth congress in February. He said the gathering aimed to build the strongest army and accelerate what he called a Korean-style military revolution by training the strongest companies, and he called for units able to carry out any combat mission on their own. The remarks followed September 21 land-mine blasts inside the Demilitarized Zone that wounded three South Korean soldiers, two of them seriously, and fueled a dispute over the inter-Korean boundary. A joint investigation by the South Korean military and the U.N. Command concluded that North Korean antipersonnel mines planted south of the Military Demarcation Line caused the explosions and that their placement violated the Korean War armistice. Pyongyang has denied responsibility and, in a letter to the U.N. Security Council earlier this week, called the incident fabricated by Seoul. South Korea on Friday asked for military talks to clarify the line's location, restore communication channels and prevent accidental clashes. Seoul says North Korean troops doing border fortification have repeatedly crossed the line, prompting warning broadcasts and warning shots, and that many original boundary markers have deteriorated or disappeared. On Wednesday, Unification Minister Chung Dong-young urged the North to accept the talks. In remarks read by a senior ministry official at a peace forum in Goyang, and reported by Yonhap, he said confrontation only escalates tensions and does no good for either side.
Ranks: soldiers and residents along the inter-Korean border · commanders ordered to prepare to fight, after three South Korean soldiers were wounded · talks are proposed and not yet accepted Source: [upi.com](https://www.upi.com/Top_News/World-News/2026/10/28/Kim-Jong-Un-prepare-for-war-border-tensions/2931793180593/)

**Budget 2026 live: chancellor says scrapping gas standing charges will save 60% of homes £45 a year: The Guardian**
Britain's chancellor, John Healey, says a budget plan to scrap gas standing charges would save 60 percent of homes £45 a year, as he prepares the first budget of Andy Burnham's government. Nesta's Andrew Sissons welcomed the step, saying it takes a chunk off energy bills and can make a switch to electric heating a better deal for some households that use more gas.
Ranks: British households that pay a gas standing charge · a claimed saving of £45 a year for 60 percent of homes · the budget is being delivered today Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/live/2026/oct/28/budget-2026-latest-updates-john-healey-andy-burnham-labour-uk-politics)

**Mapping the siege of Yemen’s Taiz, and the price families are paying: Al Jazeera**
Three weeks into the siege of Taiz, Yemen's third-largest city, Al Jazeera reported that prices have doubled and families are down to the basics.
Ranks: families inside besieged Taiz · prices doubled and diets cut to basics · the siege is already three weeks old Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/28/mapping-the-siege-of-yemens-taiz-and-the-price-families-are-paying?traffic_source=rss)

**Qatari mediators present Iran with new deal to end the war, official says: Reuters**
Qatari mediators have presented Iran with a new deal to end the war, an official told Reuters, a proposal rather than a signed end to the fighting.
Ranks: parties to the Iran war, if the offer is real · a proposal was presented, not an agreement · no acceptance date is in the report Source: [reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/qatari-mediators-present-iran-with-new-deal-end-war-official-says-2026-10-28/)

**Canada signs trade deal with UAE in push for non-US markets: Al Jazeera**
Canada has signed a trade deal with the United Arab Emirates aimed at cutting tariffs, reducing red tape and improving market access for businesses in both countries.
Ranks: businesses in Canada and the United Arab Emirates · a signed deal aimed at lower tariffs and easier access · the signing is already done Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/28/canada-signs-trade-deal-with-uae-in-push-for-non-us-markets?traffic_source=rss)

**Serbian police shoot dead assailant at Israeli Embassy: DW**
Serbia's interior minister, Ivica Dacic, says Belgrade police shot dead a minor who attacked a guard at Israel's embassy with knives, and he declared the highest terror alert.
Ranks: the dead minor, the wounded guard, and embassy staff in Belgrade · one person killed and the top terror alert set · the alert is in force now Source: [dw.com](https://www.dw.com/en/serbian-police-shoot-dead-assailant-at-israeli-embassy/a-79782905?maca=en-rss-en-world-4025-rdf)

### Both Sides: Who can form Israel's next government
The question before Israel's president, once official totals are in, is which leader has the best chance to assemble a governing coalition, usually at least 61 of 120 lawmakers. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's case, as he put it to supporters, is that Likud emerged as the largest party and that Israel must form a strong right-wing government. He effectively ruled out the two Arab parties that exit polls projected at 17 or 18 seats, so his path is a right-wing majority or a deal with opponents he has spent the campaign against. Gadi Eisenkot's case is the one he stated past midnight: the public wants change. He has called Netanyahu unfit to lead, and The New York Times reported that his voters despise the prime minister, which is the strongest reason a unity government would be hard even if the numbers required it. Eisenkot and his partners have also balked at including the Arab parties, France 24 reported it is not clear other opponents of Netanyahu would join those parties for a majority, and Eisenkot has floated a minority government instead. The Guardian reported that Itamar Ben-Gvir's Otzma Yehudit, part of the current right, was projected to stay on six seats rather than grow. President Isaac Herzog invites a leader only after seats are allocated. Counting is expected to last days, and hundreds of thousands of special-station ballots are not in the exit polls. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/live/2026/10/27/world/israel-elections)

### Progress Watch
Officials say a local ceasefire in the devastated Ukrainian city of Oleshky has held into a second day, its first 30 hours. The White House said First Lady Melania Trump secured the pause, brought forward from October 29 to Tuesday so aid could enter and a civilian evacuation could be prepared, and expanded beyond Oleshky inside the Kherson region for humanitarian convoys. She said the remaining population is mostly elderly people who need medicine, food and clean water, on mined roads under regular military attacks, and that civilian leaders from both countries would visit homes, with residents free to go to Russia or to Ukraine. Source: [english.aawsat.com](https://english.aawsat.com/world/5334588-local-ukraine-ceasefire-holds-second-day)
Source: [audacy.com](https://www.audacy.com/knss/news/world/russia-ukraine-ceasefire-melania-trump-0f135e71101c48ccd83927efeebf3347)
Source: [presidentialprayerteam.org](https://www.presidentialprayerteam.org/2026/10/28/first-lady-melania-trump-secures-humanitarian-russia-ukraine-ceasefire-in-oleshky/)

# Omni View Top World News
> **7.3 million Israelis vote today on Netanyahu's survival and the country's direction.**

**What You Need to Know:** 7.3 million Israelis are eligible to vote Tuesday in an election that puts Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's political survival on the line and is widely described as the most consequential in the country's history. Finland's and Norway's leaders also spoke directly with Vladimir Putin about ending the war in Ukraine, ahead of talks expected in Abu Dhabi in early November. This edition draws on 1 of the 5 Omni View regional desks live by press time.

### The Ten
**Israeli election puts Netanyahu’s political survival on the line: The Globe and Mail**
In Israel, voters cast ballots Tuesday in the first national election since the Hamas-led attacks of October 7, 2023, a vote many see as a referendum on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and one widely described as the most consequential in the country's history. The Israeli Central Election Committee said 7.3 million Israelis are eligible, about 330,000 of them for the first time, and the Central Elections Committee said turnout was 16.7 percent by 10 a.m., three hours after polls opened at 7 a.m., higher than in recent general elections. Polls close at 10 p.m., and The New York Times reported an immediate verdict on the next prime minister is unlikely, because opinion polls suggest Mr. Netanyahu's allies and rivals are roughly tied and assembling a coalition could take weeks or months. Mr. Netanyahu, 77, seeks re-election at the head of a coalition of nationalists and ultra-Orthodox parties that the Times called the most far-right government in Israeli history; a fractious opposition is loosely led by Gadi Eisenkot, a former military chief of staff whose son was killed in the Gaza war. The Times reported that Mr. Netanyahu's coalition offers a more religious Israel with a tighter grip on the West Bank and Gaza, while opponents cast the vote as a last chance to preserve democracy and have pledged a reckoning over October 7 and a crackdown on Israeli extremist violence against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank. President Trump has endorsed Mr. Netanyahu, the Times reported, saying anyone else would be the "wrong leader"; The Globe and Mail reported that Mr. Netanyahu said Sunday Mr. Trump was prepared to act again to remove what he called the Iranian threat only if Mr. Netanyahu remained in power, while Mr. Eisenkot accused him of a campaign of fear-mongering, lies and threats and said he was confident Mr. Trump would work with any leader the people chose. Mr. Netanyahu has resisted an independent commission on the October 7 attacks and has vowed to continue overhauling the judiciary, a move critics say could undermine liberal democracy, the Times reported. Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza cannot vote, and the Times reported that Palestinians in the West Bank are under an Israeli military lockdown as Israelis vote. The Israel Democracy Institute's Viterbi Family Center found 13 percent of Israeli voters still undecided, and The Globe and Mail reported that if neither side forms a government in the 120-seat parliament, Mr. Netanyahu could remain caretaker until another election next year.
Ranks: about 7.3 million Israeli voters, plus Palestinians who cannot vote · who governs, and policy on war, courts and the West Bank · polls close tonight; a coalition may take weeks or months Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/live/2026/10/27/world/israel-elections/heres-the-latest)
Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/world/article-israel-election-netanyahu-eisenkot/)

**Finnish and Norwegian leaders hold rare ‘frank and substantive’ call with Putin on Ukraine: The Guardian**
In Europe, Finland's president, Alexander Stubb, and Norway's prime minister, Jonas Gahr Støre, spoke by phone with Russia's president, Vladimir Putin, about the war in Ukraine. Stubb's office said the call was a follow-up to US-Ukrainian talks that Støre hosted in Oslo last week, and that the aim was to convey messages directly to Mr. Putin on future negotiations to help end the war. The office said the call was related to meetings expected in Abu Dhabi in early November among Russia, Ukraine and the United States. The statement said Finland and Norway border Russia, are firm supporters of Ukraine, and did not speak on behalf of Europe as a whole. It said the two countries highlighted a shared interest in stability in the Baltic Sea region and the High North. After the call, Mr. Stubb called the discussions "frank and substantive" and said ending the war requires direct discussions with Russia. Mr. Støre said the war carries enormous human and material costs that will affect generations, and that they stressed the importance of de-escalation. Agence France-Presse reported that Mr. Stubb and Mr. Støre were then briefing Ukraine's president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, on the talks.
Ranks: people living through the Ukraine war, plus Finland and Norway as neighbours · a direct channel into talks, not a ceasefire · Abu Dhabi meetings expected in early November Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/oct/27/russia-ukraine-oleshky-serbia-france-europe-latest-news-updates)

**Moscow gas summit draws Iran and Qatar leaders for Putin talks: Minute Mirror**
In Russia, President Vladimir Putin opened a diplomatic week in Moscow that includes the eighth summit of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum and separate talks with the leaders of Iran and Qatar. The Kremlin said both meetings sit alongside the forum and that no agreements have emerged yet. Iran's president addresses the summit on Tuesday; Tehran said his talks with Mr. Putin will centre on economic ties and regional and global issues, after Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov's visit to Tehran on October 19. Iran's acting oil minister, Hamid Bovard, listed Tehran's priorities as talks on developing gas fields, swapping gas, shielding energy facilities in wartime and aligning export policies, which Minute Mirror said are negotiating priorities, not finished deals. Aides said Mr. Putin will also hold bilateral meetings with the leaders of Mozambique and Libya, with Turkmenistan and South Africa as guests, and will speak on supply stability against a projection that global gas demand will grow 28 percent by 2055, with a "Moscow Declaration" expected. On October 28 and 29, Moscow hosts the third Russia-Africa Summit, with 48 countries taking part, 22 at the highest level, and 24 bilateral meetings for Mr. Putin, including Egypt's Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, Ethiopia's Abiy Ahmed and Congo's Denis Sassou Nguesso. Voice of Emirates reported that trade between Russia and Africa reached 27 billion dollars in 2025, and that 33 intergovernmental agreements are set to be signed.
Ranks: gas producers and importers, plus African governments in Moscow this week · talks on supply, payments and security, with no deals yet · Iran and Qatar meet Putin today; the Africa summit runs Wednesday and Thursday Source: [minutemirror.com.pk](https://minutemirror.com.pk/moscow-gas-summit-draws-iran-651712/)
Source: [voiceofemirates.com](https://www.voiceofemirates.com/en/politics/2026/10/27/putin-leads-a-diplomatic-marathon-in-moscow-hosting-a-gas-summit-and-meetings-with-24-african-leaders/)

**AI-driven disinformation running rampant on social media before US midterms, experts warn: The Guardian**
In the United States, experts told The Guardian that social media feeds are awash with AI-driven disinformation ahead of November's midterm elections, and that many posts are likely slipping through the cracks. The Guardian reported that companies including Meta have scaled back efforts to protect voters from election-meddling lies, after layoffs in trust and safety teams that followed a backlash over speech restrictions. Former Facebook engineer Frances Haugen said an information operation that was impossible at this quality in 2016 can now be run "super, super cheap," and that small tweaks can get posts past moderation. In Texas, a false claim that Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico was in a mental health facility in Ohio spread while he was home with the flu; his campaign released security-camera video of him at home, and he said he had never been to Ohio. The Digital Democracy Institute of the Americas tracked the lie as it mutated in conservative Spanish-language media into a false claim that he had attempted suicide. DDIA's Roberta Braga said platforms enforce terms of service more in English than in Spanish, and that a shift toward AI moderation and community notes means more is likely slipping through. Meta and X did not respond to requests for comment; YouTube said all users are subject to the same guidelines. Mr. Talarico's Republican opponent, Ken Paxton, earlier this year launched an advert using AI-generated footage of Mr. Talarico supposedly rewriting the Bible.
Ranks: tens of millions of American midterm voters · false claims can spread for days before a correction catches every version · voting is in November; campaigns are responding now Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/27/ai-disinformation-social-media-midterm-elections)

**RCMP probe potential fraud, money laundering in Alberta health care procurement controversy: The Globe and Mail**
In Canada, the RCMP is investigating fraud, breach of trust and money laundering connected to Alberta's health-care procurement controversy, according to a letter filed in court. The letter, dated October 15 and signed by Ontario Crown prosecutor Tom Andreopoulos, is the first public account of the potential offences police are examining. It says his office is providing advisory support and would prosecute any charges from the investigation into procurement at Alberta Health and Alberta Health Services. The Mounties confirmed in early 2025 that they had opened an investigation and earlier this year executed searches. Former Alberta Health Services chief executive Athana Mentzelopoulos sued the government and the health authority in February 2025 for wrongful dismissal, alleging pressure from government officials to drop an internal investigation into contracting and ties between private businesses and senior officials. The government says it fired her because she failed to execute its vision for the health system. None of the allegations have been tested in court. Justice Michael J. Lema ruled last month that most disputed records were privileged or confidential and ordered her to return or destroy them; Mr. Andreopoulos wrote that the Crown will ask the Alberta Court of King's Bench how to handle privilege review of seized materials.
Ranks: patients and staff in Alberta's health system, and officials under investigation · a criminal probe is now described in court, with no charges tested · the privilege fight continues in Alberta court Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/article-rcmp-probe-potential-fraud-money-laundering-alberta-health-controversy/)

A drone strike killed at least 21 people and injured 40 at a market in northern Nyala, in Sudan's Darfur, a resident said.
Ranks: shoppers and residents in Nyala · at least 21 dead and 40 injured · the strike was Monday evening Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/27/drone-strike-kills-at-least-21-and-injures-40-in-sudans-nyala?traffic_source=rss)

British prosecutors charged Mohmed Abdulkarim and Nouman Essghir, both 24, under the National Security Act over a September incident near RAF Fairford.

Ukraine and Russia traded deadly strikes Tuesday even as both said a local ceasefire had begun in occupied Oleshky.
Ranks: civilians in Oleshky and in cities still under fire · a local truce started; killing continued elsewhere · the pause is in effect today Source: [themoscowtimes.com](https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2026/10/27/russia-and-ukraine-trade-deadly-strikes-as-oleshky-ceasefire-begins-a94092)

NBC News reports Gulf states worry the United States could pull most troops from the region after the Iran war.
Ranks: Gulf governments and US forces based there · a possible drawdown, still described as a worry · no dated withdrawal in the report Source: [nbcnews.com](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/national-security/gulf-states-worry-us-pull-troops-region-iran-war-rcna604349)

### Both Sides: Should Britain reopen free movement with the EU?
What is being decided is whether the United Kingdom will treat a return to free movement as an option in a long-term relationship with the European Union. Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds said British officials have begun discussions with the EU about that long-term relationship, which could include free movement, while the near-term focus is a November summit meant to ease some trading restrictions and reach a youth mobility deal. He said Prime Minister Andy Burnham wants as little uncertainty as possible and will set out options and trade-offs after the summit. Mr. Reynolds said no assumptions have been made and no decision would be made without voters having a say. "The British people are the boss on this," he said. Mr. Burnham, in a Sunday Times interview, called for an honest discussion and said staying out of free movement would no longer be a red line. He said rejoining the single market and accepting free movement could be done without another referendum if Labour put it in its manifesto, while fully rejoining the EU would need another in-out poll.

Nigel Farage, leader of Reform UK, said discussing freedom of movement would be "very, very poor indeed." His reason is mandate: he said that five months ago Mr. Burnham told leave-voting Makerfield he would not reopen these arguments, and that two and a half years ago Labour won a large majority saying it would not re-enter the single market or the customs union or open a debate on free movement of people. Labour MP Melanie Onn, whose seat is in the north, said the scars of the post-referendum debate have not healed and that this is an unnecessary conversation now. The next dated step Mr. Reynolds named is the November summit; he said Mr. Burnham will set out the longer-term options after it. Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/oct/27/uk-eu-relationship-talks-summit-free-movement-jonathan-reynolds)

# Omni View Top World News
> **Five drone strikes cut power for residents across three Sudanese states.**

**What You Need to Know:** Five drone strikes by Sudan's Rapid Support Forces cut power for residents across three army-held states in the east, a government official said. Algeria's parliament approved the country's first foreign troop deployment since the 1970s, to Niger, to protect energy sites. This edition draws on 1 of the 5 Omni View regional desks live by press time.

### The Ten
**Sudan paramilitary drone strikes cause mass power cuts in eastern states: The Guardian**
In Sudan, the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces launched a coordinated drone attack on five power stations, a government official told The Guardian. The drones hit two stations in Al-Jazira, two in Gedaref and one in White Nile, all states the official said are held by the Sudanese army, and cut power across large parts of those three states. The official spoke on condition of anonymity. The army and the Rapid Support Forces, former allies, have been at war since April 2023. The United Nations has warned that repeated attacks on power stations threaten health care and other services for millions of people already facing what it calls the world's largest hunger crisis. In Al-Fao, in Gedaref, resident Babiker Youssef said the power had been out since early morning and that his diabetic son's insulin has to be stored in a fridge. A United Nations tally says drone strikes killed more than 300 people and injured hundreds more in the first three weeks of October. Aid workers estimate the war has killed more than 200,000 people in a country of an estimated 50 million; The Guardian reports that most hospitals have been forced to close and that at least 8 million children are out of school. In Al-Junaid, in Al-Jazira, farmer Abdelhafez Daafallah, 54, said a station the militia had destroyed was repaired and power had started to improve three months ago, then was hit again, blocking irrigation pumps he hoped would let him farm. In Gedaref, grocer Ibrahim Mohammed, 37, said he faced losing refrigerated chicken or selling it at any price, and The Guardian reports the currency lost more than 25 percent of its value in recent weeks.
Ranks: residents across three eastern states, in a country of about 50 million · electricity, medicine, irrigation and shop stocks at risk · immediate Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/26/sudan-paramilitary-drone-strikes-rapid-support-forces-power-cuts-eastern-states)

**Algeria to send troops to Niger in first foreign deployment in over 50 years: France 24**
In Algeria, both houses of parliament on Sunday approved sending troops to neighbouring Niger, the first foreign deployment of Algerian forces since troops went to support Egypt in the 1973 Arab-Israeli war, France 24 and Al Jazeera reported. The upper house approved the proposal with all 148 members in attendance voting yes, a legislator told AFP; the lower house said it voted by an absolute majority. The deployment is to protect energy facilities, and Senator Belkacem Boulghiti told the Associated Press, as carried by Al Jazeera, that troops would protect Algeria's economic interests, particularly Sonatrach oil facilities in Niger. Niger faces persistent attacks by armed groups, including near the 960-kilometre desert border, and the neighbours have agreed to deepen cooperation against jihadist violence, cross-border crime and trafficking. The vote followed Wednesday's visit by Niger's defence minister, Salifou Modi, who met President Abdelmadjid Tebboune and army chief Said Chengriha; Algerian reports said a military cooperation protocol was signed. On October 3, Tebboune said in a televised address, "We will protect Niger no matter what," and said agreements in oil, mining and other sectors were at stake. Al Jazeera reported that nearly two months ago Algeria sent four Russian-made Sukhoi Su-30 jets, a transport aircraft and an aerial refuelling aircraft to Niamey after what Algerian authorities called an attempt to destabilise Niger's military-led government, and France 24 reported that Algiers had gifted four military helicopters. A 2020 constitutional amendment requires two-thirds backing in parliament for troops abroad; Al Jazeera cited the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute as putting Algeria's 2025 military spending above 25 billion dollars, the most in Africa. Researcher Abdellah Akir told AFP the decision breaks a non-intervention doctrine, is tied to securing the Trans-Saharan Gas Pipeline from Nigeria through Niger toward Europe, and signals Morocco and the United Arab Emirates, countries with which Algiers no longer has diplomatic ties.
Ranks: people along the Algeria-Niger border and on a planned gas route to Europe · a first troop deployment abroad in more than 50 years · as soon as the force moves, timing not set in the votes Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/africa/20261026-algeria-to-send-troops-to-niger-in-first-foreign-deployment-in-over-50-years)
Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/26/algerias-military-deployment-to-niger-whats-behind-the-move?traffic_source=rss)

**Saudi Arabia confirms January start for Asian Cup 2027 despite attacks: Al Jazeera**
In Saudi Arabia, the 2027 Asian Cup will start on January 7 in Riyadh, where the hosts face Palestine in Group A, under a schedule the Asian Football Confederation announced Monday, Al Jazeera reported. The final is set for February 5 at Riyadh's 72,000-seat King Fahd Sports City Stadium, which also hosts the opening match, and 51 matches will be played over 29 days at eight venues, five in Riyadh, two in Jeddah and one in Al-Khobar. The local organising committee said it is sticking to the original schedule, although AFC chief Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa said this month that a postponement until 2028 was possible if necessary. Japan Football Association president Tsuneyasu Miyamoto said that, based on the news, the situation was still unsafe and that he did not think it would be easy to hold the cup there, adding that Saudi officials told him safety of players, fans and everyone attending was the top priority. Earlier Monday, Dakar Rally organisers said the 2027 race would be moved out of Saudi Arabia because of recent developments in the region. The Saudi-led coalition intercepted a barrage of projectiles from Yemen on Sunday, and Saudi Civil Defence said shrapnel from two intercepted ballistic missiles, suspected to have been fired by Yemen's Houthis, fell in Jeddah, Taif, Rabigh and Wadi Al-Mughammas in Mecca province. Several major events have been cancelled or postponed amid escalating Houthi attacks; international flights from King Khalid International Airport were set to resume from Terminal 2 on Sunday, with Terminal 1 for domestic flights, after suspensions that followed strikes including one on October 10 that killed 13 people and wounded hundreds. Several of the 24 participating federations have raised security concerns; defending champion Qatar opens against Thailand on January 11, the same day Japan plays Indonesia, and Saudi Arabia is hosting the Asian Cup for the first time, seven years before the 2034 World Cup.
Ranks: players, fans and residents in Riyadh, Jeddah and Al-Khobar, plus 24 national teams · a confirmed January tournament amid missile and drone attacks · January 7, 2027, unless organisers later change course Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/10/26/saudi-arabia-confirms-january-start-for-asian-cup-2027-despite-attacks?traffic_source=rss)

**Mississippi's maternity deserts deliver a political crisis: The Globe and Mail**
In the United States, a new report from the non-profit March of Dimes finds that nearly half the counties in Mississippi are maternity deserts, meaning there is no obstetrician, no family physician who delivers babies, no nurse midwife, and no hospital or clinic, The Globe and Mail reported. Michael Warren, the organisation's chief medical and health officer, said this is the result of deliberate policy decisions and resource allocations. He said 17 percent of the state's counties are one clinician away from having no one to provide obstetric care, so the state risks still more maternity deserts. The Globe reports that more infants die in Mississippi than in any other state, and that too many mothers die of pregnancy-related causes as well. Women travel long distances to a hospital, which the paper says can make prenatal appointments less likely and the trip for delivery harder. In Cleveland, Mississippi, Pam Chatman, 57, gives away baby supplies at her store, Boss Lady4Kids, through a partnership with 4 Good Community, and she has delivered fruit and vegetables to expectant mothers because people in the area struggle with obesity, diabetes and high blood pressure, which she treats as risks in pregnancy. She created Boss Lady Economic Planning and Development Workplace Transportation to offer free rides from the rural Delta to FedEx work in Memphis, and during the pandemic she helped deliver vaccines. The Mississippi Delta, in the state's northwestern corner along the Mississippi River, is known as the birthplace of the blues and the civil rights movement, and the paper describes neighbours filling gaps where services are scarce.
Ranks: pregnant women, mothers and infants across Mississippi, especially Delta counties · travel, missed care and the country's highest reported infant deaths in that state · already in force, with more counties one clinician from losing care Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/world/article-midterms-us-2026-mississippi-maternity-care-reproductive-rights/)

**Questions or concerns about voting? Text them to Colorado Newsline.: Colorado Newsline**
In the United States, more than 730,000 Coloradans had returned ballots by Friday ahead of the November 3 election, a pace Colorado Newsline says is set to rise significantly from the 2022 midterms, using secretary of state data. The paper says voters are set to deliver a verdict on two years of Republican control of the federal government under President Donald Trump and Republican majorities in Congress, and that tens of millions of dollars in campaign spending have flowed into Colorado congressional races that will help determine control of the House. Elections officials in Adams County, which includes the more Democratic-leaning half of the battleground 8th Congressional District, were notified last week that Trump's Department of Justice plans to send election monitors. Federal officials characterised that step as routine observation; Newsline reports it has raised alarm among state and local leaders. The paper also reports that, nationwide, Trump and his allies have launched a mid-decade gerrymandering push and preemptive legal challenges against some states, amid growing fears the administration could interfere with the election or refuse to accept the results. From now until Election Day and beyond, Coloradans can text NEWSLINE to (844) 494-7778 with questions on eligibility, registration, counting and certification, and Newsline staff will monitor the line.
Ranks: Colorado voters, and House control beyond the state · monitors in one battleground county and a faster early-ballot pace · now, through November 3 Source: [coloradonewsline.com](https://coloradonewsline.com/2026/10/26/text-hotline-2026-election-questions/)

**Aleksandar Vucic Concedes Defeat in Serbian Election: The New York Times**
In Serbia, Aleksandar Vucic said it is clear his party lost Sunday's snap election after 12 years in power.
Ranks: Serbian voters after a near-record political break · a conceded loss, not yet a new government in these reports · immediate Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/25/world/europe/serbia-vucic-election-defeat.html)

**Lula's defeat of Bolsonaro in Brazil denies Trump an ally: The Globe and Mail**
In Brazil, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won a fourth term with 51.8 percent to Flávio Bolsonaro's 48.2 percent, The Globe and Mail reported, and Bolsonaro called for the election to be annulled, The New York Times reported.
Ranks: Brazilian voters and governments watching Brasília · a certified-court win the loser rejects · immediate Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/world/article-brazil-election-lula-da-silva-flavio-bolsonaro/)
Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/live/2026/10/25/world/brazil-election)

**More than 2,600 Palestinians displaced as Israeli army continues large-scale offensive in Hebron: Anadolu Ajansı**
In the West Bank, Israel's offensive in Hebron has displaced more than 2,600 Palestinians, Anadolu reported.
Ranks: more than 2,600 displaced Palestinians in Hebron · loss of homes during an ongoing offensive · already underway Source: [aa.com.tr](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/more-than-2-600-palestinians-displaced-as-israeli-army-continues-large-scale-offensive-in-hebron/4101003)

**Crowds welcome Venezuela's María Machado after months in exile: BBC World**
In Caracas, opposition leader María Corina Machado returned after more than 10 months in exile, having left by speedboat, and thousands of supporters greeted her.
Ranks: Machado's supporters in Caracas · a return after more than 10 months away · Sunday's welcome Source: [bbc.co.uk](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/videos/cwgkv8kmly4zo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)
Source: [dw.com](https://www.dw.com/en/venezuela-opposition-leader-machado-returns-from-exile-received-by-thousands-of-supporters-in-caracas/a-79759187?maca=en-rss-en-world-4025-rdf)

**Uganda's central bank warns of speculation as government halves non-essential spending: IntelliNews**
In Uganda, the government has halved non-essential spending, and the central bank has warned of speculation.
Ranks: Ugandans dependent on non-essential public spending · a cut by half, with a speculation warning · now Source: [intellinews.com](https://www.intellinews.com/uganda-s-central-bank-warns-of-speculation-as-government-halves-non-essential-spending-478816/?source)

### Both Sides: Should the 2027 Asian Cup stay on its January dates in Saudi Arabia?
The Asian Football Confederation and Saudi organisers have published a January and February schedule for the 2027 Asian Cup, while attacks on the kingdom and a rival event's exit have put that choice under challenge. The case for going ahead is that the local organising committee is sticking to the original dates, that the AFC has now announced a full match calendar, and that Saudi officials told Japan Football Association president Tsuneyasu Miyamoto their top priority is the safety of players, fans and everyone attending. AFC chief Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa has already said a postponement until 2028 is possible if necessary, which leaves a formal off-ramp rather than an open-ended commitment. The case against keeping the dates is Miyamoto's: based on what he had learned from the news, the situation was still unsafe, and he did not think it would be easy to hold the cup there. Dakar Rally organisers, earlier Monday, moved the 2027 race out of Saudi Arabia because of recent developments in the region. Saudi Civil Defence said shrapnel from two intercepted ballistic missiles, suspected to have been fired by Yemen's Houthis, fell on Sunday in Jeddah, Taif, Rabigh and Wadi Al-Mughammas, and the kingdom has faced waves of Houthi missile and drone attacks, including an October 10 strike that killed 13 people and wounded hundreds and led to a suspension of flights at Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport. Several of the 24 federations have raised security concerns. The next dated step on the published schedule is the January 7 opening in Riyadh, unless the AFC uses the postponement option Al Khalifa described. Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/10/26/saudi-arabia-confirms-january-start-for-asian-cup-2027-despite-attacks?traffic_source=rss)
