# Omni View Top World News
> **Nearly one thousand arrests followed marches by hundreds of thousands across France over living costs.**

**What You Need to Know:** Nearly one thousand people were arrested in France after Saturday’s marches over living costs and schools, with the interior ministry and the unions far apart on how many turned out. Serbians vote in a snap parliamentary election, British Columbia has a Conservative majority, and Storm Boelo is still disrupting the northern United Kingdom.
This edition draws on 1 of the 5 Omni View regional desks live by press time.

### The Ten
**Almost 1,000 arrested as clashes follow another day of mass protests across France: BBC**
France saw clashes late Saturday after another day of protests over the cost of living and poor school conditions. The interior ministry estimated 410,000 people marched; the unions put the number at about 800,000. Police fired tear gas and water cannon in cities including Paris after largely peaceful demonstrations, barricades were set alight in Marseille, and people ripped boards from a shop in Bordeaux. Some 70,000 officers were deployed after President Emmanuel Macron decreed earlier this week that only demonstrations organised by recognised trade unions would be permitted. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said, in remarks reported by AFP, that several thousand radical activists gathered at the rear of the Paris march, including around 500 people identified as rioters. The Interior Ministry said 142 people were arrested in the capital, less than half the number on the same day last week, after last weekend’s unrest became some of the worst disorder in modern French history. Nuñez said two people were seriously injured, one in Toulouse and one in Clermont-Ferrand; Franceinfo reported that a 20-year-old protester in Toulouse had several fingers torn off when a nearby explosive went off. Authorities in Bouches-du-Rhône said seven businesses had been looted or damaged. A Paris protester who gave her name as Zelie told the BBC people were frustrated and had been suffering since Macron came to office.
Ranks: Hundreds of thousands of marchers and residents in French cities · arrests, injuries and street damage · already, from Saturday into Sunday Source: [bbc.co.uk](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c95ynd587ynzo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)

**Serbia votes in election pitting longtime leader against student movement: Al Jazeera**
Serbia began voting Sunday in snap parliamentary elections called by Aleksandar Vucic in September. The vote follows almost two years of student-led demonstrations after 16 people died when a train-station canopy collapsed in Novi Sad in 2024, a disaster widely blamed on government corruption. Vucic, prime minister and then president for more than a decade, resigned the presidency in September to run again for prime minister. Al Jazeera describes a country of six million; France 24 puts the electorate at 6.4 million, choosing among 18 parties for a 250-seat parliament. Vucic has promised higher pensions and public-sector salaries, investment in state health care and subsidies for young couples, and has kept ties with China and with Russia, Serbia’s main gas supplier, while leaving the door open to the European Union. The Student List, led by cardiologist Ilija Srdanovic, fields 250 largely unfamiliar candidates and says its priority is rooting out corruption and restoring the rule of law. Vucic and his Serbian Progressive Party deny repression, corruption and spying, and he claims the students are funded by foreign agents in Croatia and Montenegro, a charge the students deny. About 150,000 student-movement supporters rallied in Belgrade on Thursday. Polls close at 8 p.m. local time, with first indications expected about two hours later; France 24 says the state election commission is not expected to release the official tally before Monday. Vucic has said his side would concede if it lost, and has also warned that protests alleging fraud if his party wins would be quashed.
Ranks: Serbia’s voters, about six million people · who forms the next government · indications Sunday night, official tally from Monday Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/25/serbia-votes-in-election-pitting-longtime-leader-against-student-movement)

**British Columbia Conservatives win a majority and David Eby resigns: The Globe and Mail**
Canada’s British Columbia has elected a Conservative majority for the first time in nearly a century. With 95 percent of polls reporting, The Globe and Mail said 64 Conservatives, 27 New Democrats and two Greens were elected. David Eby resigned as NDP leader, accepting responsibility for an election he called two years early, and said the result ends nine years of NDP rule, four of them under him. He told supporters the party would serve as official opposition and cited recruiting family doctors, helping to lower rents and raising the minimum wage. Interim Conservative leader Lorne Doerkson, in his victory speech, pledged to boost the economy, cut red tape, freeze all provincial taxes, triple natural gas production over nine years and hold an international investment summit in Vancouver, with health care fully and publicly funded. He said repealing the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act would be among his top priorities; Indigenous leaders have opposed any changes to that law. He also told First Nations the future would be built as partners, and told the crowd he believed in private property rights and parks open to all British Columbians. Green leader Emily Lowan was elected in Saanich North and the Islands, and Jeremy Valeriote was re-elected in West Vancouver-Sea to Sky. The province faces a continuing trade war with the United States, Doerkson’s backdrop as he takes office.
Ranks: British Columbia’s voters and the incoming government · a change of governing party after nine years · immediate, on a reported majority Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/article-bc-election-david-eby-ndp-lorne-doerkson-conservatives/)

**Bulgaria holds presidential elections amid divisions over Ukraine war: DW**
Bulgaria is voting Sunday for a president, a largely ceremonial post that can still appoint interim governments, command the armed forces and veto legislation. Incumbent Iliana Iotova, who took office this year after Rumen Radev left the presidency and became prime minister, favors dialogue with Moscow to bring peace to Ukraine and opposes military aid to Kyiv. Her main challenger, former caretaker prime minister Andrey Gyurov, is backed by the pro-Western opposition, criticizes Radev’s foreign policy and supports Bulgaria’s Euro-Atlantic ties as a European Union and NATO member. Kostadin Kostadinov of the pro-Russian Vazrazhdane party is also running; DW says 27 candidate pairs are on the ballot and nearly half are openly pro-Kremlin. The war is a central theme after four merchant ships were allegedly hit by drones off the Bulgarian coast this month, and after Starlink antennas were set on fire near Sofia. Radev has said the attacks seemed to advantage Russia and summoned the Russian ambassador; his government has declined to blame the incidents directly on Moscow. Rising energy prices, inflation and corruption are also issues in the EU’s poorest member state. Polls are open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m., official results can take up to 48 hours, and a runoff is scheduled for November 1 if no candidate wins an absolute majority.
Ranks: Bulgarian voters and Ukraine-war policy in an EU and NATO state · who holds the presidency and its veto · Sunday’s vote, with a possible November 1 runoff Source: [dw.com](https://www.dw.com/en/bulgaria-holds-presidential-elections-amid-divisions-over-ukraine-war/a-79753496?maca=en-rss-en-world-4025-rdf)

**Storm Boelo: warnings in place in Scotland, Northern Ireland and north of England as high winds batter UK: The Guardian**
The United Kingdom took a second named storm in two days as Storm Boelo followed Friday’s Storm Austen. The Met Office said winds in the amber zone, in force from 9 p.m. Saturday, reached 60 to 70 mph, with gusts above 80 mph on exposed coasts, including 82 mph on Tiree in the Inner Hebrides at about 4 a.m. Sunday. Chief forecaster Jason Kelly said the strongest winds and greatest disruption risk were in the north, and warned of danger to life from flying debris and crashing waves; people were told to stay indoors and secure loose items. Gusts of 50 to 60 mph were possible elsewhere, with heavy rain adding a hazard in the north and risks to travel and power. Liverpool’s River of Light and London’s Diwali on the Square were cancelled, Edinburgh Castle is closed Sunday, and Fountains Abbey in North Yorkshire closed for the day. Flooding blocked the railway between Preston and Blackpool North, trees came down near Dumfries, and hundreds of flights were delayed or cancelled at Dublin, Heathrow, Manchester, Edinburgh and Glasgow. By 7 a.m. Sunday the Environment Agency had 66 flood alerts and 10 flood warnings in England; Cumbria police reported flooding and fallen trees. Hundreds of homes in south-west England were still without power after Austen, which brought 76 mph winds at St Mary’s airport in the Isles of Scilly.
Ranks: People across Scotland, Northern Ireland and northern England · travel, power and a stated danger to life · through Sunday, with warnings already in force Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/oct/25/storm-boelo-warnings-scotland-northern-ireland-north-of-england-high-winds-uk)

### Both Sides: Who is responsible for an AI-assisted strike on a school?
Vox reports that on the first day of the United States war against Iran, a strike on an elementary school killed 123 children. The strikes were ultimately approved by humans and facilitated by the Maven Smart System, Palantir software that aggregates battlefield data. Operators fed Maven intelligence that classified the school as an Iranian military facility; the site had been converted into an elementary school in 2017, and that intelligence did not reflect the change. Some reporters have called it one of the worst massacres by the US government since the Vietnam War. The open question is who bears responsibility when humans and a machine are both in the chain.

Some US Central Command personnel, according to Pentagon officials who spoke to Bloomberg, expected Maven to flag stale information or inconsistencies in the target intelligence. Their case is that the system should have caught the bad classification before the school was marked a priority target for day one.

A Palantir spokesperson told Bloomberg the company is not responsible for the underlying data or for identifying intelligence deficiencies, and denied that the evidence showed its software was at fault. Stanford law lecturer Allen Weiner, a former State Department lawyer, says one legal theory puts war-crimes responsibility on manufacturers because of the code, while another says that does not hold, especially if the military has said the tool may not make substantial autonomous judgments. No dated next step is set out in the article; the dispute as reported is between those Pentagon officials’ expectation and Palantir’s denial. Source: [vox.com](https://www.vox.com/future-perfect/507570/ai-weapons-war-crime-responsibility)

# Omni View Top World News
> **Fifty percent each leaves Brazil's presidency tied two days before Sunday's vote.**

**What You Need to Know:** Fifty percent each leaves Brazil's presidency tied two days before Sunday's vote, after a Friday debate in Rio de Janeiro between President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Flávio Bolsonaro. A Datafolha survey published Thursday put the pair level, after Bolsonaro had led by four points in polls published two weeks earlier, and the first round on October 4 had given him 47 percent to Lula's 45 percent. This edition draws on 1 of the 5 Omni View regional desks live by press time.

### The Ten
**Brazil’s Lula and Bolsonaro debate policy proposals before run-off: Al Jazeera**

Brazil's presidential run-off reached its last televised argument on Friday in Rio de Janeiro, with voters due to choose on Sunday between the incumbent and a senator who finished ahead of him in the first round. Al Jazeera reports that President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and his right-wing rival, Flávio Bolsonaro, questioned each other about the economy, infrastructure and regional development. The debate was broadcast on TV Globo. Al Jazeera calls Friday's exchange notably more diplomatic than the candidates' initial face-off on Sunday, and also a debate that still carried personal attacks and tense moments. The New York Times, in a same-day report, identifies Flávio Bolsonaro as the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro and says the former president was jailed over a coup plot. That identification is background the Times states. It is not a finding about who will hold the office after Sunday, and no outlet in today's file predicts the result.

The count that put the two men in a run-off is already on the record. Bolsonaro finished first in the initial round of voting on October 4 with 47 percent of the vote to Lula's 45 percent. A Datafolha institute survey published on Thursday suggested the pair are now tied with 50 percent support each, compared with Bolsonaro's four-point lead in polls published two weeks ago. Al Jazeera's summary line says polls indicate the candidates are neck and neck before Sunday's voting. What the same article does name as the last campaign step is street politics: both candidates are expected to join supporters in Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo before Sunday's run-off.

The policy argument, as Al Jazeera records it, turned first on the size of public spending. Lula challenged his rival's plan to take a "chainsaw" to public spending in a manner similar to that of Argentina's president, Javier Milei. Bolsonaro answered in these words: "I'll have the same job here [as Milei in Argentina] because you're leaving the country bankrupt." His stated case is that the country he would inherit is bankrupt, and that the remedy is the spending cut he associates with Milei. Lula's challenge is to that plan. The report does not set out a line-by-line budget from either side. It places the chainsaw image and the bankruptcy reply at the centre of the economic exchange.

Bolsonaro, described as the son of former right-wing president Jair Bolsonaro, then accused the incumbent of allowing organised crime to expand, driving families into debt, and not addressing the higher cost of living. Those three charges are the case he made, in the order Al Jazeera gives them: crime, then household debt, then prices. Lula, whom the report calls Brazil's first working-class president, answered the personal edge of that attack with, "He doesn't know what hunger is." Bolsonaro replied, "Why are things so expensive?" The cost-of-living argument therefore sits in the record as an exchange. Lula questioned the senator's experience, saying, "He doesn't know Brazil." His challenger doubled down on presenting himself as a capable candidate who represented change for the country. Experience against change is the second fight the debate left with viewers, beside spending and crime.

Three tense exchanges followed, and each is a claim by a named person, not a court finding. Bolsonaro called Lula "Nine Fingers," a pejorative nickname Al Jazeera says is used by many of his supporters and that references an accident the president suffered during his time as a metalworker. Lula, described as 80, demanded an apology. Bolsonaro gave it. The nickname and the apology are both in the report.

Lula in response called Bolsonaro a vigilante, referring to allegations that his rival has ties to paramilitary groups in Rio de Janeiro. Bolsonaro said he would classify those groups as "narcoterrorists." The allegation of ties is reported as an allegation Lula referred to, not as a conviction. Bolsonaro's reply is his stated classification of those groups, not a judicial outcome. One candidate alleges paramilitary ties and uses the word vigilante. The other says he would classify those groups as narcoterrorists.

The third tense exchange was between Bolsonaro and the mother of a five-year-old who was killed in a shootout that involved a policeman who had the presidential candidate as his lawyer. Bolsonaro said he does not believe his client was guilty. The policeman is described only as someone involved in that shootout and as Bolsonaro's client. He is not described here as guilty. Bolsonaro's statement is a belief about his client, given in the debate, not a verdict. The mother's presence is part of what Al Jazeera calls the third tense moment.

Friday's record is therefore a debate that opened on policy and also put character, crime and a lawyer-client claim in front of a national audience. Voters were asked to weigh a proposed cut in public spending, modelled in Lula's challenge on Milei's approach and defended by Bolsonaro as the job of a country he says is being left bankrupt. They were asked to weigh Bolsonaro's charges that organised crime has expanded, that families have been driven into debt, and that the higher cost of living has not been addressed, against Lula's replies on hunger, prices, and whether his rival knows the country. They were also asked to weigh a nickname and an apology, an allegation of paramilitary ties against a promise to label those groups narcoterrorists, and a candidate's statement that he does not believe a former client was guilty.

The people who change something by acting are Brazil's voters, in a national run-off, on Sunday. How much changes is the occupancy of the presidency and, on the candidates' own terms in Friday's debate, the direction of spending, the handling of organised crime and the cost of living, and the experience they say the office requires. How soon is Sunday, two days after the Rio debate and after the street campaigning both sides are expected to hold in Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo. This account records the debate, the Datafolha reading, and the first-round count. It does not award the weekend to either candidate.

Ranks: Brazil's voters in a national presidential run-off · the presidency and the spending, crime and cost-of-living course the candidates argued · Sunday's vote Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/24/brazils-lula-and-bolsonaro-debate-policy-proposals-before-run-off?traffic_source=rss)
Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/24/world/americas/flavio-bolsonaro-brazil-election-president.html)

### Both Sides: New Jersey's voter-roll cleanup before early voting
New Jersey began early voting Saturday while officials and campaigns fight over who stays on the rolls, in the same window that New York also opened early voting. Democracy Docket reports that millions of voters across both states are preparing to cast ballots as disputes over voter eligibility, mail voting and federal access to voter data have intensified in the final weeks before Election Day. The question in New Jersey is whether correction of a Motor Vehicle Commission software error, and Ocean County's residency review, should keep running through those final days, or stay narrow enough that eligible voters are not swept into a cleanup or a challenge.

House Republicans make the case for more records and more scrutiny. On Wednesday they subpoenaed acting Secretary of State Shirley Emehelu, a Democrat, for additional documents about the glitch, arguing the state's response has been inadequate. The subpoena came after New Jersey refused to provide personally identifying information about the affected voters, and after the Department of Justice lost its own lawsuit seeking broader voter-registration data from the state in July. The underlying error, as the state describes it, ran from June 2023 to June 2024: roughly 6,600 people who answered "no" when asked whether they were U.S. citizens were nevertheless marked as citizens by the state's software and transmitted for voter registration. Republicans' stated reason for pressing now is that the response so far has not been enough, and that the immediate ballot-access question is whether efforts to correct the rolls remain limited to ineligible registrations.

Governor Mikie Sherrill, a Democrat, and voting-rights groups make the case for a narrow fix. Sherrill said fewer than 400 people who were newly registered because of the error later voted. The state says those votes did not affect any election. It has spent months removing registrations that resulted solely from the error, while separately reviewing people who may have another valid registration or evidence of eligibility. In Ocean County, a separate dispute tests how far local officials can go in questioning residency just before an election. The county Board of Elections has been investigating dozens of Democratic and unaffiliated voters in Bay Head whose property-tax bills are sent outside the borough. Voting-rights groups sued, alleging the process discriminated against those voters while excluding similarly situated Republicans. A judge declined last week to halt the investigation, allowing the review to continue. Their reason is that a last-minute cleanup, or a partisan residency challenge, can catch eligible voters, force them to prove eligibility shortly before an election, and expose them to extra scrutiny at the polls or even after Election Day. The dispute involves only a few dozen voters, but Democracy Docket says the mechanism has broader implications. Early voting is already under way. Both New York and New Jersey are also preparing to count mail ballots that are lawfully cast on time but may arrive after Election Day, a process the report says could again become a target of misinformation if close congressional races remain unresolved. Source: [democracydocket.com](https://www.democracydocket.com/news-alerts/new-york-and-new-jersey-start-voting-as-ballot-access-fights-intensify/)

### Progress Watch
Ukraine's defence ministry says Starlink and its military version, Starshield, are again recording speeds over 400 kilometres per hour, with a stable connection, after more than a week of restrictions. Defence minister Evhenii Khmara told reporters that monitoring systems are recording a return to normal speed for Starlink and Starshield, and that the connection is stable. The ministry said speed metrics that had shown disruptions have now returned to normal. The restrictions were first reported on October 14. Ukrainian officials said they undermined Ukraine's ability to intercept Russian attack drones and disrupted frontline communications. Sources said connection speeds had been reduced to about 160 kilometres per hour or less. The New York Times describes Starshield as the Pentagon-funded satellite network that Ukraine relies on to thwart Russian attacks, and says the announcement followed more than a week of disruption. France 24 reports that neither SpaceX boss Elon Musk nor the United States government has acknowledged responsibility for restricting Starlink or Starshield in Ukraine, and that both have said publicly that any such decision could only have been taken by the other. Reuters has reported that the order to throttle Starshield came from inside the White House. President Donald Trump said on Friday that if problems with access to Starlink communications systems in Ukraine persisted, he would "get it straightened out." Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20261024-ukraine-says-starlink-and-starshield-connection-stable-again)

# Omni View Top World News
> **Two soldiers dead near Hebron, Israel orders a West Bank-wide closure before Tuesday's election.**

The White House says a local pause in occupied Oleshky will open a humanitarian corridor on October 29, while gunmen killed mourners at a church funeral in Jordan and a Paris-suburb attack is under a terrorism inquiry. This edition draws on 1 of the 5 Omni View regional desks live by press time.

### The Ten
**Netanyahu orders ‘very extensive’ operation in West Bank after two Israeli soldiers killed: The Guardian**
In the occupied West Bank, the Israel Defense Forces said two Palestinian gunmen opened fire on Friday at a temporary checkpoint outside Hebron after failing to reach a nearby highway, where the military believes they had meant to attack civilians. The Globe and Mail named the dead soldiers as Staff Sgt. Ron Yonatan Roytman, 23, and Sgt. Yuval Shai Svilem, 20, and said three other Israelis were lightly wounded; The Guardian reported that a preliminary military investigation found the gunfight lasted more than 20 minutes and left five Israelis wounded, two of whom later died. The army said both Palestinians, from Hebron and armed with an M16 and a handgun, were killed near the Yehuda Junction, and an AFP photographer who witnessed the battle saw two men with a handgun and an automatic rifle exchanging fire. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s office said it had ordered Hebron cordoned off at once and a full closure of the West Bank from Friday, the fourth such territory-wide restriction in a month, shutting gates that link Palestinian villages to major roads while Israeli drivers, including settlers, can still pass. Netanyahu said forces would evacuate residents of the attackers’ neighbourhood, go house to house, seize weapons and destroy what he called terrorist infrastructure, on a scale he described as unseen in the West Bank for decades, using a model the army applied in the “Iron Wall” operation that the UN rights office says forcibly displaced tens of thousands from northern refugee camps from January 2025. He blamed Hamas for “planning a major attack aimed at murdering innocent civilians”; army chief Eyal Zamir said a large quantity of ammunition found in the gunmen’s vehicle was meant for a larger attack, and the army said dozens of operations afterward led to dozens of arrests, including people affiliated with Hamas and Islamic Jihad, and the seizure of M16 rifles and submachine guns. Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich called for a West Bank campaign “exactly like in Gaza,” including dismantling the Palestinian Authority, collecting weapons and eliminating those he called terrorists, and said that would be among the first demands of the next government. National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir said Palestinian freedom of movement should be restricted because the lives of settlers, soldiers and police “are a million times more important.” Former Peace Now director Yariv Oppenheimer told Al Jazeera that demolitions, curfews, arrests and settler revenge attacks were likely, and that daily life for Palestinians was already impossible. Israeli voters decide next Tuesday whether Netanyahu gets another term, three years after the Hamas-led attacks that triggered the Gaza war.
Ranks: Palestinians across the West Bank and Israeli voters · a territory-wide closure and a threatened house-to-house campaign · starting Friday, with an election next Tuesday Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/23/netanyahu-orders-very-extensive-operation-west-bank-two-israeli-soldiers-killed) · [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/world/article-israel-orders-west-bank-closure/) · [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/23/world/middleeast/west-bank-shooting-israel.html)

**Melania Trump brokered ceasefire at besieged Ukrainian town, White House says: The Washington Post**
In Russian-occupied Oleshky, in Ukraine’s southern Kherson region, the White House said on October 23 that First Lady Melania Trump had helped broker a local ceasefire so aid can enter and civilians can leave. The White House said Ukraine and Russia agreed to pause military action, with the ceasefire set for October 29, and that she and a representative negotiated timing, technical procedures and implementation directly with both leaderships as what it called an “Exclusive Intermediary.” Melania Trump said the town is “a front-line war city on the brink of disaster,” that those left are “primarily elderly” and urgently need medical attention, medicine, food and clean water, and that without her intervention aid and evacuation of the elderly “would be impossible.” UNITED24 Media reported the White House estimate of 1,700 to 2,000 residents still there, mostly elderly, plus about 50 children, against about 24,000 before the full-scale invasion, and said no comprehensive census has been taken since 2022. It also said about 90 percent of the city flooded when the Kakhovka Dam collapsed in June 2023. Under the announced plan, civilian representatives from both sides would visit homes to assess needs, people who choose to leave would get transport either to Ukrainian-controlled territory or to Russia, an independent American media organization would document the process so residents’ preferences are respected, and the sides would coordinate demining because roads remain contaminated with explosives. The White House did not say how long the pause would last or how compliance would be monitored. The Guardian said there was no comment yet from Moscow or from Ukraine, and that its correspondents were still trying to corroborate the statement. Ukrainian Human Rights Commissioner Dmytro Lubinets said on October 23 that talks on evacuations were still under way, though nearing completion, and UNITED24 Media said Ukraine had not officially confirmed the deal. Russia and Ukraine have each accused the other of blocking supplies since May, a stretch linked by the White House and The Guardian to deaths from starvation and disease, a destroyed morgue, problems burying bodies, and no running water. Pope Leo XIV urged Vladimir Putin on October 16 to accept a ceasefire so food and medicine could reach civilians. By October 19, Kyiv and Moscow were moving to finish an evacuation from Oleshky and six nearby settlements, where around 6,000 civilians, including up to 200 children, were believed to remain. The White House tied the channel to earlier contacts that, it said, returned seven Ukrainian children on April 2, 2026, and five more on July 30 in a fifth such reunion.
Ranks: roughly 1,700 to 2,000 people still in Oleshky, mostly elderly · a dated pause for aid and a choice of evacuation route, if both armies honour it · ceasefire set for October 29 Source: [washingtonpost.com](https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2026/10/23/melania-trump-secured-ceasefire-besieged-ukrainian-town-white-house-says/) · [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/oct/23/starlink-ukraine-musk-trump-russia-black-sea-strikes-france-milan-europe-protests-latest-news-updates) · [united24media.com](https://united24media.com/world/us-announces-russia-ukraine-ceasefire-deal-for-civilian-evacuations-in-temporarily-occupied-oleshky-23754)

**Six shot dead by gunmen at church funeral in Jordan, officials say: BBC World**
In Jordan, government spokesman Mohammad al-Momani said gunmen killed six people and wounded 28 others on Friday at a church funeral in the village of Hmoud, in the Karak governorate. France 24’s account of the Public Security Directorate placed the shooting at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak, about 180 kilometres south of Amman. Al Jazeera reported at least seven killed, and said survivors described two masked men opening fire as dozens attended the funeral procession. Mourner Khaled Burqan told al-Mamlaka television that two attackers, with a rifle and a pistol, fired for several minutes inside a church where dozens had gathered; BBC-verified CCTV appears to show three armed men moving from a road toward the church, two entering what looks like a vehicle entrance, retreating, then returning with a third, all apparently carrying handguns. Separate footage the BBC said appeared to be from the aftermath showed dead and wounded on the ground. Al-Momani called the attack heinous, said security forces were deployed and were investigating, and said the prime minister would chair a Security Council meeting attended by all ministers, with an interior-ministry briefing expected shortly. No one had claimed responsibility. The unidentified gunmen were reported to have arrived by car, opened fire, and fled, and a manhunt was under way. Karak has a sizeable Christian community in majority-Muslim Jordan. The BBC noted that such violence is rare, though deadly attacks have occurred before; in 2016, gunmen ambushed police in Karak, including at a Crusader castle popular with tourists, killing 10 people, seven of them officers, before security forces killed the gunmen after a long standoff.
Ranks: the funeral congregation and Karak’s Christian minority · six or at least seven dead and 28 wounded, with attackers still sought · Friday, with a security meeting the same day Source: [bbc.co.uk](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ck87zlpzny15o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss) · [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/23/at-least-seven-killed-after-gunmen-open-fire-at-church-in-jordan?traffic_source=rss)

**Deadly shooting near Paris investigated as 'crime of terrorism', minister says: BBC World**
In France, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said a series of drive-by shootings on Friday in Trappes, southwest of Paris, and then in nearby La Verrière killed one person and wounded five others, three of them seriously, in a rampage of almost 15 minutes. France 24 reported one killed and four wounded, including a 12-year-old girl, and said authorities suspect the attack may have been racially motivated. The New York Times said the shooter fired from a car in several locations southwest of the capital and that antiterrorism prosecutors were exploring a racial or religious motive. The National Anti-Terrorist Prosecutor’s Office said the case appeared to be murder in connection with a terrorist enterprise, including the aggravated circumstance of acts committed because of real or perceived membership of a particular race, ethnicity, nation or religion, and Nuñez told reporters in Trappes that it was clearly a terrorist crime. Trappes Mayor Ali Rabeh said an individual fired shots from his vehicle at several people he encountered, at a petrol station, a medical centre, a playground and several vehicles, wanting “as many casualties as possible” and to “cause carnage”; witnesses said the car was a grey Renault Clio. Rabeh said the person killed was of African origin and one person in critical condition was of North African descent, and called the attack racist and probably Islamophobic, while the anti-terror prosecutor urged caution on the victims’ identities. A local police chief told BFMTV the suspect used an older-style semi-automatic weapon in bursts; Le Parisien reported the gun dated to the Second World War. The prosecutor’s inquiry also covers possession of a Category A weapon, which includes military-grade weapons or weapons that can fire in bursts, and conspiracy with a terrorist group to prepare crimes against people. The suspected attacker, a 39-year-old known to police but not to France’s intelligence services, local media reported, was arrested; Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu’s statement placed that arrest in nearby Coignières, and a police union official said the suspect was detained on the N10 in La Verrière. The motive, Nuñez said, remained unclear.
Ranks: residents of Trappes and La Verrière, including a wounded child · one dead and four or five wounded, now a terrorism case · Friday morning, suspect already held Source: [bbc.co.uk](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6ev38dj1g8zo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss) · [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/suspect-arrested-after-1-killed-and-4-wounded-in-a-shooting-in-paris-suburb) · [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/23/world/europe/france-shooting.html)

**French authorities tighten restrictions and ban specific protests: France 24**
In France, President Emmanuel Macron is set to meet student-union representatives on Friday, the first such meeting since the mobilisation began, as the government prepares for Saturday’s protests by high-school pupils whose complaints over school conditions grew into a wider movement. France 24 reported that Paris is extending a partial curfew in parts of the city until Monday, that protests are banned altogether in Marseille and Lyon, that 70,000 security personnel will be deployed on Saturday, and that only union demonstrations will be authorised. The Globe and Mail reported that those 70,000 police officers and gendarmes would be deployed with helicopters, armoured vehicles and water cannons, and that the Louvre and major Paris museums will close on Saturday over concerns about violence. The measures follow weekend looting and clashes that injured police officers and damaged stores, which authorities are trying not to repeat; authorities have also banned some student protests and called for videos of looting to identify rioters. Paris Saint-Germain’s game was postponed after a police request amid the protests, Al Jazeera reported, and Ousmane Dembélé is to miss the Ballon d’Or event because of that move. Shop owners have been preparing for the weekend in fear of riots. Aaron Rodgers of the Pittsburgh Steelers said the NFL would cancel Sunday’s Paris game against the New Orleans Saints in Saint-Denis, about 10 kilometres from where Saturday’s protests are expected, if the city were unsafe. The meeting with students is a scheduled talk, not an agreement yet announced. France’s 10-year government bond yield has pushed above 5 percent for the first time since 2002 as debt fears grow, France 24 reported, with a Moody’s verdict awaited and a downgrade widely expected.
Ranks: people in Paris, Marseille, Lyon and other protest cities · curfews, city bans, closed museums and 70,000 officers on the streets · Saturday’s mobilisation, curfew through Monday Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/french-authorities-tighten-restrictions-and-ban-specific-protests) · [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/world/article-france-saturday-protests-police-louvre-closed/) · [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/10/23/dembele-to-miss-ballon-dor-event-as-psg-game-moved-amid-protests-in-france?traffic_source=rss)

**Russia and Ukraine swap 270 prisoners each: Reuters**
Russia and Ukraine each swapped 270 prisoners of war, Russian state media told Reuters.
Ranks: 540 freed prisoners and their families · release from captivity · announced Friday Source: [reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russia-ukraine-have-swapped-270-prisoners-war-each-russian-state-media-reports-2026-10-23/)

# Omni View Top World News
> **Forty-four contacts are isolated to stop Nigeria's first Ebola case in over a decade from spreading.**

**What You Need to Know:** Forty-four contacts are isolated to stop Nigeria's first Ebola case in over a decade from spreading. Tehran says seven tankers were damaged overnight in the Strait of Hormuz, and missiles struck Kyiv after talks. This edition draws on 1 of the 5 Omni View regional desks live by press time.

### The Ten
**1. Nigeria's first Ebola patient holidayed in Uganda, officials say: BBC World**
Nigeria has its first confirmed Ebola case since the East African outbreak began in May: the wife of a diplomat based in Abuja, who travelled to Kampala for a holiday, Dr Jean Kaseya of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention told the BBC.
She is originally from Uganda, and she fell ill three days after arriving home in the Nigerian capital on 3 October.
Health Minister Muhammad Ali Pate told the BBC the patient is 42, spent two and a half weeks in Kampala, and made a two-hour stopover in Ethiopia's capital on the return; he said she is stable and improving.
She tested positive on Tuesday. Pate said authorities had identified 44 people who had contact with her, not all of them close, because the net was cast wide.
Aviation Minister Festus Keyamo said 46 people — 44 who met her at hospital and two who worked in her home — are banned from boarding flights, and Nigeria has added airport health screenings, temperature checks, movement tracking and digital health declarations.
Neighbouring Cameroon has also stepped up surveillance at its airports and ports.
Pate said none of the contacts now in isolation are known to have symptoms, including the person she travelled with, and that she has not travelled outside Abuja since landing.
Kaseya said symptoms began on 6 October, that she first sought care thinking she had malaria, and that she was admitted to a second private hospital on the 11th. Pate said public health authorities were alerted on 19 October and three laboratory tests confirmed the diagnosis the next day.
She has the Bundibugyo species, the same as the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, which the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control reports has claimed at least 4,600 lives, with more than 9,500 cases. That species has no approved vaccine or treatment, though trials are under way. The incubation period is two to 21 days.
Uganda, where at least two people died after the outbreak was also reported there, declared itself free of the disease in August after its last patient was discharged.
Ranks: Nigeria's contacts and travellers, dozens of people · a first case in over a decade is being ring-fenced · isolation is in force now Source: [bbc.co.uk](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c62kepvg2x9lo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)

**2. Iran says 7 oil tankers damaged in Strait of Hormuz as fears of all-out war return: The Globe and Mail**
Seven oil tankers caught fire or were damaged overnight in the Strait of Hormuz after being hit by Iran or striking naval mines, Tehran said Thursday, in the war that began with United States and Israeli attacks on 28 February.
Iranian state television reported those claims, citing the Revolutionary Guard Corps navy, which again threatened to strike United States military bases in the region if the United States keeps guiding commercial ships through the strait.
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations did not report the attacks. Monitors have noted reluctance by some shippers to report incidents. Iran still asserts control of the waterway.
Iran's top diplomat, Abbas Araghchi, said on Wednesday that Tehran remains open to diplomacy but is ready to defend itself. In recent days Tehran has indicated it could expand targets to undersea cables and data centres.
The United States is sending a third aircraft carrier and thousands of troops, joining the largest force of American warships and aircraft in the Middle East in decades.
Iran is still promoting a proposal that would end the war and fully open the strait within a week if the United States ends its blockade of Iranian ports, conditions that echo a deal that fell apart within days of being signed in June.
President Donald Trump rejected that seven-day proposal. Both sides have acknowledged that indirect discussions have continued, and attacks on ships in the strait have increased since the rejection.
A return to all-out war would again endanger civilians across the region and complicate deliveries of oil, natural gas and fertilizer, with Israel's elections days away and United States midterms next month.
Ranks: shippers and oil-importing countries worldwide · seven tankers damaged and the strait's leverage higher · overnight, with talks still indirect Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/world/article-iran-us-strait-of-hormuz-ships-damaged/) Source: [wlwt.com](https://www.wlwt.com/article/iran-oil-tankers-fire-damaged-fears-return-war/74213820)

**3. Russian strikes hit Kyiv after Witkoff meets Putin: Al Jazeera**
In Ukraine, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said three waves of ballistic missiles, 21 in all, had been launched at Kyiv by Russian "humanitarians" since yesterday evening, answering United States peace envoy Steve Witkoff's praise of Vladimir Putin as "a humanitarian".
He said ordinary residential buildings, energy facilities, infrastructure at a railway station and the metro, shopping malls, businesses and a monastery were damaged, and that twelve regions came under Russian attack overnight.
Zelenskyy said at least two people died and 34 were injured in Kyiv, including five children, and that emergency services were working at the affected sites.
Al Jazeera reported Ukraine's toll for the capital as one killed and 22 injured, and reported the strikes after Witkoff met Putin.
Zelenskyy said the attack came almost immediately after another round of talks, that there had been no real change in Russia's attitude, and that real pressure on Russia was needed for steps toward ending the killing.
Ukraine said appeasement will not end the war, Al Jazeera reported.
Ranks: people in Kyiv and twelve Ukrainian regions · homes, energy sites and a station hit, with dead and injured · overnight, just after talks Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/oct/22/france-protests-emmanuel-macron-ukraine-energy-attacks-latest-europe-news-updates) Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/22/russian-strikes-hit-kyiv-after-witkoff-meets-putin?traffic_source=rss)

**4. Experts alarmed by 'less transparent' CDC as US measles deaths rise: The Guardian**
In the United States, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention added a third measles death to its dashboard on Wednesday and would not say whether it was in Pennsylvania or another state.
Confirmed cases grew by 8% in one week to 4,410 so far this year, nearly double last year's count.
A Department of Health and Human Services spokesperson told the Guardian that privacy laws and legal restrictions mean the National Center for Health Statistics cannot identify the state or give further details, and did not answer which laws those were.
Dorit Reiss, a professor of law at UC Law San Francisco, said naming a state would not give personal details, and that nothing prevents giving death numbers by state. Lindsay Wiley, a professor at UCLA Law, said the agency is guided by the Federal Privacy Act, not Hipaa, and that the ban applies to information that reveals an individual's identity.
Debra Houry, former chief medical officer at the CDC, said the agency still has access to other systems, including NNDSS, and that Pennsylvania's privacy laws would not limit reporting a state and deaths.
Pennsylvania has reported six deaths, the most recent still under investigation by state officials. The CDC dashboard lists three deaths this year despite five confirmed deaths in Pennsylvania.
Reiss called it a change from past practice and said the CDC is being less transparent than in the past.
Ranks: people facing a US outbreak of 4,410 cases · a third death logged while the state is withheld · this year, up 8% in a week Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/22/cdc-measles-pennsylvania-state-deaths)

**5. Commentary: The Arizona-Nevada-California water war is heating up, and all three states will end up parched: Los Angeles Times**
Arizona has moved to join Nevada's federal lawsuit against a United States Interior Department plan that cuts Colorado River water for Arizona, Nevada and California, the downstream basin states, through 2028, with harsher cuts over the following eight years.
Nevada sued to block the plan in late August. Arizona told the court its interests are unique and that it cannot entrust them to another state suing to protect its own.
California, the largest consumer of Colorado River water, has not expressed an interest in joining the lawsuit.
Lake Mead and Lake Powell are at their lowest levels since they began filling. As they fall further, Hoover and Glen Canyon dams could lose the capacity to provide water and power downstream.
The government got the three states to agree to reductions over the next two years: through 2028, California is to cut use by about 12%, Arizona by 31% and Nevada by 28%.
After that, total allotments to the three states could be cut by as much as 40% through 2036.
The 1922 Colorado River Compact guaranteed the lower three states at least 7.5 million acre-feet a year. A Los Angeles Times commentary argues the engineering estimate used to support that guarantee was a lie, not a mistake, because it rested on a short, unusually wet sample of the river's flow.
Ranks: water users in Arizona, Nevada and California · cuts of about 12 to 31 percent, then possibly 40 percent · through 2028, and on to 2036 Source: [latimes.com](https://www.latimes.com/business/story/2026-10-22/the-arizona-nevada-california-water-war-is-heating-up-and-all-three-states-will-end-up-parched)

In Yemen's Taiz, government forces launched hundreds of strikes on Houthi locations, a spokesperson said, as the UN warns nearly 260,000 people are now displaced.
Ranks: displaced people in Yemen, nearly 260,000 · strikes and displacement continue · now Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/22/fighting-rages-in-yemens-taiz-as-un-warns-nearly-260000-now-displaced?traffic_source=rss)

In New Mexico, Meta has been fined $25 billion, accused of misleading users on data privacy linked to the Cambridge Analytica scandal.

Swiss and Austrian aid workers, held over a year in Niger, were freed in Libya and are due to fly home Thursday.
Ranks: two aid workers and their families · more than a year of captivity ended · they fly home Thursday Source: [bbc.co.uk](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cq62y0v7434yo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)

**10. Persian Gulf oil pollution doubles during Iran war, research finds: CNN**
Satellite oceanographers at the University of South Florida say oil pollution on the Persian Gulf's surface has doubled during the Iran war.
Ranks: marine life in the Persian Gulf · surface oil pollution has doubled · measured during the war Source: [cnn.com](https://www.cnn.com/2026/10/22/climate/video/persian-gulf-oil-pollution-doubles-during-iran-war)

### Both Sides: California's one-time billionaire tax
Californians vote early next month on Proposition 40, a one-time 5% tax on the roughly 250 billionaires who live in the state. Meta, the company behind Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, has struck a deal with chief executive Mark Zuckerberg to keep him a resident of California, or wherever Meta keeps its base, for eight years even if the tax passes. He would receive new non-voting shares, created by a two-for-one split for all shareholders, that could be sold to pay a potential multibillion-dollar bill without diluting his control. Zuckerberg, worth $239bn according to Forbes, told Meta he was considering moving his primary residence because the measure could force him to sell voting shares.

The case for the tax, as Congressman Rohit Khanna of California's 17th district put it, is that every society is taxed and the only question is who pays. He argues that working people pay more than they should while billionaires are becoming trillionaires, and that billionaires should pay what he calls their fair share so working people are unburdened. He has called the vote a choice between standing with the working class or the oligarchs.

The case against, as Zuckerberg put it to his own company, is that the bill could be large enough to force a sale of the shares that control Meta, or a move out of the state where the headquarters sit. Sergey Brin, Peter Thiel and Eric Schmidt are among tech billionaires spending heavily to fight the measure. Recent polling has shown Proposition 40 still short of majority support. The next step is that vote early next month. The result is not known.

### Progress Watch
China's crude oil imports from the Gulf rose 25.7% in September from the month before, to 13.8 million tonnes, a third straight monthly increase, Chinese customs data show, after months of disruption from the war on Iran. Xu Muyu, a senior crude analyst at Kpler, said demand for Middle Eastern crude was likely to remain strong amid record drawdowns, and that China's increased buying of Saudi crude was driven by a sharp rise in Saudi supplies to Asia and pricing that makes those barrels highly competitive. Source: [scmp.com](https://www.scmp.com/economy/global-economy/article/3371778/chinas-gulf-oil-imports-forecast-approach-pre-iran-war-high-shipments-rebound)

# Omni View Top World News
> **Russia freed seventy-four-year-old Stephen Hubbard as Witkoff brought Putin a Ukraine peace proposal.**

**What You Need to Know:** Russia freed seventy-four-year-old Stephen Hubbard as Witkoff brought Putin a Ukraine peace proposal, and after the St. Petersburg meeting Witkoff said a foundation for a ceasefire exists. Kenya is treating its first Ebola outbreak, Gulf oil exports have moved above pre-war volumes, and Britain has approved the Jackdaw gasfield for supply from the end of the month.
This edition draws on 1 of the 5 Omni View regional desks live by press time.

### The Ten
**Putin hosts Trump envoy Witkoff for Ukraine talks, frees U.S. citizen held in Russia: The Globe and Mail**
Russia hosted U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff in St. Petersburg on Wednesday for a ninth in-person meeting with President Vladimir Putin on ending the war in Ukraine, and released retired American teacher Stephen Hubbard, 74, from custody. Hubbard, from Michigan, was sentenced in 2024 to nearly seven years after prosecutors accused him of serving in a defence unit in Izyum; he denies the mercenary charge, the U.S. State Department had classified him as wrongfully detained, and Russian state media said Putin told Witkoff that Hubbard had been taken to Pulkovo Airport. The Globe and Mail reported the talks opened with that release inside the Constantine Palace, with investment envoy Kirill Dmitriev present, as Washington presses a new diplomatic push more than two years after President Donald Trump promised to end the war within 24 hours. Witkoff told Putin he had brought ideas for a peace deal; after the meeting he said the Oslo talks were constructive, that a foundation exists on which a Ukraine ceasefire can be built, and that he hopes Putin will consider trilateral talks with Kyiv on technical issues. A day earlier Witkoff met President Volodymyr Zelensky in Oslo in talks a U.S. official called constructive; Secretary of State Marco Rubio called them positive and said Witkoff would carry those ideas to Russia, while Zelensky said the meeting agreed to resolve disruptions to intelligence sharing and the Starshield satellite system. Trump said it was time for Ukraine to end the war or face "a very bad thing," and that Zelensky will have to want a deal because "I don't think his people are going to stand for it any longer." Putin, who has sought full control of Donetsk and no NATO membership for Ukraine, told Witkoff Russia is prepared to help resolve the Iran crisis and wants economic cooperation restored; he said the first shipment under this month's diesel export deal with the United States leaves in two to three days, and Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said Moscow would listen but expected no miracle. Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store said Witkoff planned to return to Oslo and that Russia may be looking for a diplomatic opening; separately, Russia said its position on an energy ceasefire is unchanged and that it seeks peace rather than a truce, while the Wall Street Journal reported Elon Musk ordered a Starshield slowdown that Reuters could not verify, Trump denied ordering restrictions, and Rubio said Washington had not pulled back Kyiv's Starlink access.
Ranks: people living through the Ukraine war, plus one freed prisoner · a new talks round and a diesel shipment, not a signed peace · this week, with fuel due in days Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/world/article-putin-witkoff-meet-for-ukraine-talks-stephen-hubbard-released/)
Source: [dw.com](https://www.dw.com/en/russia-frees-jailed-american-stephen-hubbard-us-envoy-says/a-79719452?maca=en-rss-en-world-4025-rdf)
Source: [bbc.co.uk](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6m24l9v3745o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)
Source: [kurdistan24.net](https://www.kurdistan24.net/en/story/947601/witkoff-meets-putin-in-st-petersburg-foundation-for-ukraine-ceasefire-exists)
Source: [aa.com.tr](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/eurasia/russia-says-position-on-energy-ceasefire-with-ukraine-unchanged-seeks-peace-not-truce/4095545)

**Is Ebola under control in Kenya after nine cases confirmed?: BBC**
Kenya is facing its first Ebola outbreak, with nine confirmed cases all linked to a man who travelled from the Democratic Republic of Congo and died two weeks ago, the BBC reported. Four relatives of that first patient, three health workers and a hospital cleaner have tested positive. The United States has advised its citizens to reconsider travel to Kenya, and Uganda, Ethiopia and Somalia are on alert. The International Rescue Committee says more than 9,500 cases in Congo since May, and more than 4,000 deaths, make this the second most deadly outbreak of the disease and leave Kenya exposed to further imported infections. The outbreak is the Bundibugyo species, which has no approved vaccine or treatment, though trials are under way. Health Director-General Patrick Amoth said Tuesday evening that the eight surviving patients were improving and responding to treatment. Kenya has ordered enhanced screening for travellers from ten countries it calls high risk, including digital forms and QR codes, and has designated isolation facilities and a dedicated test laboratory at Kenyatta National Hospital. Of 135 listed contacts of the first patient, 134 remain in quarantine; the International Rescue Committee said that pattern shows the early response is working, while doctors' union representative Dennis Miskellah told the BBC that border and port facilities are grossly understaffed.
Ranks: Kenyans, travellers, and neighbours of a regional hub · nine linked cases in a first outbreak, against a much larger Congo epidemic · now, while contacts stay in quarantine Source: [bbc.co.uk](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c693z948px0jo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)

**Wall Street Journal: Regional Oil Exports Exceed Pre-War Levels: IranWire**
Middle Eastern oil exports, including shipments through the Strait of Hormuz and alternative routes, have risen above pre-war levels even as attacks on shipping continue, IranWire reported from a Wall Street Journal account of Kpler tracking data. Regional exports reached over 24 million barrels a day in the week ending October 18, compared with 23.3 million before the war. Oil moving through Hormuz itself is about 14 million barrels a day, 82 percent of the previous volume. The Journal described that gap as a sign of Iran's diminished ability to stop regional oil reaching world markets, citing U.S. naval protection, ship-to-ship transfers off Oman, and pipelines in Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates. In September, about 40 percent of crude exported by Persian Gulf countries other than Iran bypassed Hormuz, up from 17 percent before the war. About 30 attacks on vessels were recorded in October, maritime security reports cited by the paper said, while the cost of moving a barrel from the Gulf to China on a very large crude carrier reached roughly $37.37 and war-risk insurance rose to as much as 10 percent of a vessel's value in some cases. High profit margins are still drawing tanker owners into the region despite drone and missile strikes. The same account said Iran's own oil exports have virtually stopped under a U.S. maritime blockade.
Ranks: oil buyers and Gulf exporters worldwide · volumes above the pre-war rate, at much higher shipping and insurance cost · already, in the latest tracking week Source: [iranwire.com](https://iranwire.com/en/news/159134-wall-street-journal-regional-oil-exports-exceed-pre-war-levels/)

**UK approves Jackdaw gasfield in North Sea: The Guardian**
The United Kingdom has approved production at the Jackdaw gasfield in the North Sea, and the government said gas will reach homes and businesses from the end of the month. Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh said she agreed the regulator can grant consent, that the field will create 27 jobs and secure 273, and that the decision supports winter energy security and is compatible with legally binding climate commitments and a 2050 net-zero target. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the step will protect hundreds of jobs and help keep millions of homes warm, arguing Britain will still need oil and gas for decades even on an ambitious climate path. Government data cited in a Guardian analysis show oil and gas supplied 75 percent of UK energy in 2025 and about 43 percent of overall energy was imported. Jackdaw, about 150 miles east of Aberdeen, is owned and operated by Adura, a venture half owned by Equinor and half by Shell; a Guardian column said it will be 6 percent of UK North Sea gas output at peak over an 11-year life. Greenpeace UK's Ami McCarthy said the approval will not lower bills, will not meaningfully add to supply, and will create just 27 full-time jobs, putting Jackdaw at around 2 percent of gas demand for roughly ten years. Uplift's Tessa Khan said the field has been oversold and that no new oil and gas fields fit safe climate limits; Green leader Zack Polanski accused Labour of climate vandalism. Fahnbulleh said the government will launch an energy wealth fund with a £2 billion down payment, and Rosebank, mostly oil, is being decided separately.
Ranks: UK households that use gas · a new domestic supply from month's end, not a promised cut in bills · this winter Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/oct/21/jackdaw-gasfield-in-north-sea-approved)
Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/business/nils-pratley-on-finance/2026/oct/21/jackdaw-approval-step-towards-grownup-north-sea-policy)
Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/politics/live/2026/oct/21/jackdaw-gasfield-labour-andy-burnham-zack-polanski-uk-politics-latest-news)

**'Hunted like animals': inside Trump's war on the people who build America: The Guardian**
The United States is running its largest immigration-arrest effort in Texas construction, where the Guardian reported more than 12,000 ICE arrests in July, almost double Florida or California. The paper said four in ten Texas construction workers are foreign born, most of them Hispanic and undocumented, and that the administration's ICE 2.0 drive is chasing a target of 3,000 immigration arrests a day. Houston immigration lawyer Jacob Monty said agents are hunting construction workers in the early morning the way hunters go after deer. The Guardian reported that house framer Lorenzo Salgado Araujo was killed by ICE agents, and that street arrests are leaving sites unfinished and pushing up house prices and grocery costs. Sergio Benavides, a naturalised citizen and home-building company owner in the Rio Grande valley who voted for Donald Trump in 2024, said a subcontractor and the man's wife were picked up by ICE and left three U.S.-citizen children. Benavides said home, food and gas prices have risen and that remaining workers must be paid more because so many have been deported. The account said Latino Texans who can vote, including some who backed Trump for the economy and the border, are angry as midterm elections approach within days. The Guardian described the shift as a move from last year's militarised operations in Los Angeles and Minneapolis to less visible stop-and-search tactics with, it said, rich pickings in Texas.
Ranks: Texas construction workers and the families around them · thousands of arrests and emptied job sites · now, with midterms days away Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/ng-interactive/2026/oct/21/trump-ice-construction-worker-deportation)

**Drone attack in disputed Sudan-South Sudan border region kills at least 153: Al Jazeera**
South Sudan says Sudan's army killed at least 153 in a drone strike on a disputed-border market; MSF is treating 20 wounded.
Ranks: people at a disputed-border market · at least 153 dead and 20 in treatment · already Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/21/drone-attack-in-disputed-sudan-south-sudan-border-region-kills-at-least-153?traffic_source=rss)

A New York Times analysis, using U.S. Geological Survey data, says Venezuela's official toll of 6,509 deaths from June's earthquakes is probably a severe undercount.
Ranks: families of Venezuela's quake dead · the official count is likely far too low · the quakes were in June; the reassessment is today's Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/21/world/americas/venezuela-earthquakes-deaths.html)

**Italy deploys army and approves tougher anti-riot laws after violence: France 24**
Italy will deploy 500 troops to Milan, and Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said ministers eased minors' detention and will fine parents for damage.
Ranks: Milan residents and minors caught in the unrest · 500 troops plus easier detention and parental fines · now Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/italy-deploys-army-and-approves-tougher-anti-riot-laws-after-violence)
Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261021-italy-deploys-troops-into-milan-in-response-to-recent-riots)

**French PM vows stronger security as country prepares for more protests: France 24**
France's Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu promised a massive police deployment, and Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said the military will reinforce security forces.
Ranks: people in French cities facing further protests · a larger police presence with military backup · for the coming protests Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/french-pm-vows-stronger-security-as-country-prepares-for-more-protests)

**Trump Wields an Unprecedented $277 Million in Final Midterm Stretch: The New York Times**
President Donald Trump's super PAC is putting an unprecedented $277 million into the final stretch of the U.S. midterm elections.
Ranks: U.S. midterm campaigns and the voters they are trying to reach · 277 million dollars in late spending · the closing stretch of the campaign Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/20/us/politics/trump-maga-inc-midterms.html)

### Both Sides: Should Britain produce gas from Jackdaw on the way to net zero?
The United Kingdom has decided to let the Jackdaw gasfield produce, with supply due from the end of the month. The question is whether that gas should be brought ashore while the government still says it will reach net zero by 2050.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham's case is that the real question is where oil and gas come from, not whether Britain will still burn them. He says the approval will protect hundreds of jobs and help keep millions of homes warm this winter, and that even on an ambitious climate path the country will need oil and gas for decades. Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh says homegrown gas this winter supports energy security, reduces use of higher-emission imports, fits legally binding climate commitments, will create 27 jobs and secure 273, and will sit beside a £2 billion down payment on an energy wealth fund for the climate transition. A Guardian analysis adds that oil and gas supplied 75 percent of UK energy in 2025, that about 43 percent of energy was imported, and that Jackdaw — 6 percent of UK North Sea gas at peak, over an 11-year life — pipes fuel into the national network.

Greenpeace UK's Ami McCarthy says there is nothing pragmatic about rubber-stamping a project that will not lower bills, will not boost energy security, and will create just 27 full-time jobs, while leaving households tied to expensive oil and gas and to petrostates. She puts Jackdaw at around 2 percent of gas demand for roughly ten years. Uplift's Tessa Khan says the field will be largely unmanned and operated remotely, will not stop the decline in North Sea jobs, and that no new oil and gas fields are compatible with safe climate limits. Green leader Zack Polanski has accused Labour of climate vandalism.

Gas is scheduled to flow by the end of the month. Rosebank, mostly oil, is still a separate decision, and the government has asked the regulator to consider other urgent tie-back fields.

### Progress Watch
